stories.headline: Nolo becomes Category 3 Hurricane in remote Pacific Ocean
stories.deck: The storm’s maximum sustained winds rapidly intensified to 115 mph (185 kph), the Miami-based National Hurricane Center reported, meaning it was a Category 3 hurricane
stories.bodyText:
Nolo strengthened into a major hurricane on Saturday (October 3, 2026) far out in the Pacific Ocean, well to the west of Hawaii’s main islands.
The storm’s maximum sustained winds rapidly intensified to 115 mph (185 kph), the Miami-based National Hurricane Center reported, meaning it was a Category 3 hurricane.
Nolo was located about 210 miles (335 kilometres) south-southwest of Maro Reef and moving westward at 17 mph (28 kph).
A tropical storm warning was issued for the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument — a massive and remote federally protected area with islands, atolls, seamounts, shoals and coral reefs — from Maro Reef to Lisianski Island.
The hurricane centre said large surf associated with Nolo “will likely inundate some of the low-lying atolls.”
No threat was in the forecast for any populated islands, however.
The hurricane centre said Nolo was expected to cross the international date line on Sunday (October 4, 2026).
Nolo skirted Hawaii as a hurricane a week ago. It then lost some of its punch and became a tropical storm before regaining hurricane strength on Friday (October 2, 2026).
Meanwhile, another Pacific hurricane, Category 1 Rachel, continued heading westward on a path away from the west coast of Mexico.
Dangerous swells were forecast through the weekend for the coast of west-central Mexico and through Monday (October 5, 2026) for the Baja California Peninsula, according to the hurricane centre.

stories.headline: ‘You’re coming in blind?’ Chilling audio before medical jet carrying 6 vanished
stories.deck: A medical evacuation jet traveling from Bermuda to Boston has gone missing over the Atlantic Ocean. The Gulfstream G100 signaled an emergency and lost contact just moments before it vanished from radar. The US Coast Guard's search efforts have located a debris field south of Nantucket, providing critical details about the situation.
stories.bodyText:
The chilling audio captures the final moments before a medical evacuation jet disappeared over the Atlantic.
The aircraft had reported an emergency and electrical problems before losing radio and radar contact. The US Coast Guard later found a debris field linked to the missing aircraft off Nantucket.
According to Reuters, the Canadian registered Gulfstream G100 operated by Latitude Air Ambulance left Bermuda’s LF Wade International Airport at around 12.41am local time on Saturday. It was headed for Boston Logan International Airport with six people on board.
Air traffic control recordings posted by LiveATC.net captured the final exchanges. The controller asked the pilot, “Roger, you said you’re coming in blind. Is that what you said?” The pilot’s response was not clearly audible. The controller then asked whether the crew was declaring an emergency.
According to the Boston Globe, the aircraft was dealing with an electrical problem shortly before contact was lost. Emergency crews at Boston Logan were told the plane had lost radio and radar contact while approaching the area south of Nantucket.
Reuters reported that the Gulfstream had been flying at around 24,000 feet before dropping about 13,000 feet in roughly two minutes. The Associated Press also reported that the aircraft descended to around 10,000 feet before contact was lost.
The rapid descent came as the aircraft approached the Massachusetts coast. The Boston Globe reported that the plane was around 80 miles south of Nantucket when emergency crews at Logan were told to prepare for its arrival. It never reached Boston.
The FAA issued a search and rescue alert at around 1.20am, according to the Boston Globe. The US Coast Guard then launched aircraft and vessels to search the waters south of Nantucket.
The Coast Guard later confirmed that it had found a “debris field” from the missing medical flight. The debris was located south of Nantucket and was confirmed to be associated with the aircraft. Search operations for the six people on board continued.
The Coast Guard said the search had covered about 1,644 square miles by the time the debris was located, according to the Nantucket Current. The discovery provided investigators with physical evidence of the aircraft’s final location.
The six people on board included two pilots, two medical personnel, a patient and the patient’s relative. The four crew members were Canadian, while the two passengers were from Bermuda, according to the Canadian Press report carried by Stratford Today.

stories.headline: Kerala orders vigilance probe into 2006 suicide case linked to CEC Gyanesh Kumar
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Kerala home minister Ramesh Chennithala has ordered a Vigilance investigation into allegations of irregularities involving Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar during his tenure as the state’s Public Works Department Secretary in 2006, news agency ANI reported.
The case concerns the death by suicide of Malaysian civil engineer Lee See Been, who was associated with the PATI-BEL consortium involved in the upgradation of MC Road under the Kerala State Transport Project. Been’s suicide note reportedly mentioned Gyanesh Kumar.
The investigation has been ordered following allegations that external pressure was exerted and that the original inquiry into the case was derailed.
Chennithala has directly instructed the Vigilance Director to conduct a thorough inquiry into the allegations of external influence in the case involving Gyanesh Kumar and take appropriate action based on the findings, the Home Minister’s Office said.
The development comes as opposition parties, student organisations and youth groups held protests in Delhi and Mumbai on Friday, demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and claims of mass voter deletions.
Around 700 people were detained in Delhi, while thousands gathered at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park despite police denying permission for the demonstrations.
In Delhi, those detained included AAP leaders Atishi, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Sanjeev Jha, AISA president Neha Bora, CPI(M) leaders M A Baby and Brinda Karat, CPI national secretary P Sandosh Kumar, RJD leader Manoj Jha, social activist Yogendra Yadav, DYFI president A A Rahim and former JNUSU president Aishe Ghosh.

The agitation intensified after media reports claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months regarding decisions and procedures linked to the SIR exercise and other electoral matters.
The reported objections covered issues including voter deletions, Form 6 and access to electoral-roll databases. The Election Commission, however, rejected suggestions that the objections reflected institutional dissent, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions raised during the draft stage were part of its routine administrative and decision-making process.
The ECI said the three-member commission had taken all decisions, including those related to the SIR, unanimously.

stories.headline: ‘We had a good debrief’: Indian head coach Craig Fulton
stories.bodyText: Kakamigahara (Japan): A winner scored with close to the last 40 seconds left on the clock might have saved the Indian men’s team from a lot of embarrassment during their 4-3 semifinal win over Pakistan. But, the mood in the camp right after the final hooter went off was certainly anything but upbeat. . The close shave was precisely the sort of game the Indians needed to pull up their socks, put their head down and play to their full potential, said head coach Craig Fulton after his team won the final and booked their 2028 Los Angeles Olympics spot on Saturday here at the Kawasaki Juko Stadium. . The Harmanpreet-led side’s gold medal-winning performance was the contrast of what they had displayed 48 hours prior on Thursday evening. Easing past world no. 12 Malaysia 5-1, the eighth-ranked India were barely tested. But unlike their previous outing, the Indians ensured their level of play never dropped. . “Well, we just had a good debrief,” shared Fulton after the comprehensive victory for gold. .Asian Games: Brilliant Pranavi Urs claims historic golf gold. “We were just honest with the way we played and I think the occasion got to us a little bit because if we didn’t get four and five goals and then you make one or two mistakes.. then Pakistan get their tail up. They can play and they can score goals and I’m glad we found a way to win that game. I think we needed to play a match like that, it helped us in this final today,” said the South African. . The team was flying into Japan after receiving a lot of flak for finishing eighth at the World Cup in the Netherlands and Belgium last month. For Fulton, evidently, the average performance in Europe still stung. But a win here, he felt, was as important too. . “Well, that was the main goal of 2026, the World Cup. Had we won the World Cup we still would have had to come here and play to win. Obviously the World Cup didn’t go the way we wanted it to so I’m glad we dominated in Asia and this was important for us.”

stories.headline: Protesters in Hyderabad demand CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, scrapping of SIR
stories.deck: The protest began with a Hindi rendition of Bella Ciao, the Italian anti-resistance song, with protesters dubbing SIR as ‘Special Intensive Resistance’
stories.bodyText:
A protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was held at Dharna Chowk in Hyderabad on Saturday (October 3, 2026), with demonstrators alleging that the exercise could exclude large sections of voters from the electoral rolls.
The protest began with a Hindi rendition of Bella Ciao, the Italian anti-resistance song, with protesters dubbing SIR as ‘Special Intensive Resistance’. The demonstration was organised by 12 organisations, including the Telangana unit of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and the Telangana People’s Front (TPF).
The three demands
The protesters raised three demands, the resignation of Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, selection of the Chief Election Commissioner through a process that includes the Chief Justice of India (CJI), and scrapping of the SIR exercise.
Speakers at the protest gathering alleged that the SIR was the National Register of Citizens (NRC) through the back door. The allegations came amid a wider national controversy over the deletion of names from electoral rolls during the revision exercise. The protesters claimed that 13 crore names had been excluded from draft electoral rolls across States and Union Territories.
M.V. Reddy, a TPF member, described the scale of the deletions as unprecedented, saying that while several electoral revisions had been carried out in the past, none had resulted in such a large number of names being removed.
Akunuri Murali, former chairperson of the Telangana Education Commission, read out the Preamble to the Constitution during the protest, with demonstrators raising their right hands and repeating the words after him. Sunita Regunta of the National Alliance of People’s Movements said the organisation had been following the SIR process since it began in Bihar ahead of the State’s elections. She alleged that the exercise was disproportionately affecting people without the resources or means to navigate the process and was removing them from electoral rolls.
Although the protest was scheduled to begin at 10 a.m., people arrived gradually, with the gathering growing to around 100 participants by 11 a.m. at Dharna Chowk.
Sameer of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) drew a parallel with the protests over the NEET question-paper leak, saying the mobilisation of Gen Z over the issue had demonstrated the impact of sustained public pressure. He called for similar mobilisation against the SIR process.
Usman, general secretary of the Association for Protection of Civil Rights (APCR), said a large section of society continued to remain unconcerned about developments in the country. He alleged that the SIR could exclude people who sought to strengthen democratic institutions and stressed that voting was a fundamental part of democratic participation.
Sreeja of the Disha Students Organisation said SIR was normally intended to increase voter enrolment but was instead being used to delete voters. She also alleged that the ruling party had concluded that Gen Z would not support it following the police lathicharge during protests in Delhi.
Kancha Ilaiah, Dalit rights activist and former Professor of political science at Osmania University, recalled the functioning of the Election Commission during the Emergency. He said the institution had remained independent even then, pointing to the subsequent election of Janata Party as an example of the importance of an independent electoral process.
Cyber security activist Srinivas Kodali raised concerns about linking different databases through the SIR process. He questioned how voter identities could be reliably established when Aadhaar itself had not been properly created for everyone, and alleged that the process could eventually be incorporated into an NRC-like exercise. Mr. Kodali also said the movement against SIR should continue even if Mr. Kumar resigned, pointing to the upcoming Census and the wider implications of linking citizens’ lives and identities to government databases.

briefs.headline: BCom student stabbed to death in B'luru: How 'feud' over senior girl turned fatal
briefs.deck: A 19-year-old BCom student named Yogesh was fatally stabbed in Nagarabhavi following a classmate's dispute. The confrontation stemmed from disparaging remarks made by Yogesh regarding a senior girl pursued by Bhuvan. After gathering a group, Bhuvan called Yogesh behind the college to confront him over these remarks. During the violent altercation, one assailant used a knife to stab Yogesh in the…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A feud between two college classmates over a senior girl turned fatal in Nagarabhavi on Wednesday, leaving a 19-year-old BCom student dead.
The deceased, Yogesh, a resident of Nagadevanahalli, was a first-year BCom student at a private college in Nagarabhavi. Bhuvan, his classmate, had reportedly been persistently pursuing a senior girl student from the same college. Tension escalated after Yogesh allegedly made disparaging remarks about the girl recently.
Group called student behind college
After learning about the remarks, an enraged Bhuvan and a juvenile allegedly assembled a group of youths from Laggere and called Yogesh to meet behind the college campus around 2.15pm. Yogesh reached the spot with a classmate, where Bhuvan and his associates confronted him over the comments.
The confrontation soon turned violent. One of the juveniles allegedly pulled out a knife, which police said had been purchased online, and stabbed Yogesh in the chest, a senior officer said.
Friends rush Yogesh to hospital
Yogesh's classmate and another friend rushed him to a nearby hospital, but doctors declared him dead. The assailants fled immediately after the attack. 
Police arrested four people, including Manoj, 19. Three of those arrested are 17-year-old juveniles and were sent to the state juvenile home, while Manoj was taken into police custody. Bhuvan, identified as the key accused, remains absconding, police said.

briefs.headline: 15.87 lakh form 7 applications before SIR, 84,900 filed during exercise: Data
briefs.deck: 15.87 lakh form 7 applications before SIR, 84,900 filed during exercise: Data
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Amid the political mudslinging between the Congress and BJP in Karnataka over alleged bulk applications for mass deletion of voters by BJP, Election Commission data shows that form 7 applications seeking deletions were significantly higher before the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) than during the exercise. . The data reveals that 15.87 lakh form 7 applications, resulting in 14.84 lakh deletions, were received between January 1, 2025 and June 16, 2026. . In comparison, only 84,900 form 7 applications were submitted between June 16 and October 2, all pending verification. . While the Congress has alleged systematic deletion of targeted voters, particularly its supporters, BJP has maintained that Congress added bogus voters to the rolls to win elections and that it was only petitioning the EC to remove fraudulent entries. .SIR: When the voter is put on trial to remain on the roll. Chief Minister D K Shivakumar has alleged a huge “conspiracy” by the BJP to delete 50 lakh voters. State BJP president B Y Vijayendra said the actual submissions were only a few thousands. . “Submitting form 7 is not illegal. The EC will verify each objection before any deletion,” Vijayendra said. . Checks and balances . Senior election officials said no voter had been deleted so far and that any unusual spike in forms 6, 7 or 8 would be easily detected as numbers are regularly tracked. . “In an election year, we see an abnormal increase in applications for voter inclusion, shifting of voters and even movement of potential candidates between constituencies or wards. Parties are aware of both additions and deletions as forms 9, 10, 11 and 11A are shared with them on the last Saturday of every month. The EC also tracks formats 1 to 8 to monitor demographics, coverage and changes,” an official said. Booth-level agents (BLAs) appointed by parties, the official said, act as concurrent auditors with access to data. . The formats provide polling station-wise gender ratio and elector-population ratio, inclusions and deletions compared with the previous roll, district-level age-cohort data, EPIC and photo coverage, polling station locations, service voters and migrated electors. EPIC is the electotral photo identity card. . Officials also pointed to low net deletions, with forms 7 and 8 being interlinked. . In June, 14.84 lakh names were deleted, 6.96 lakh voters shifted and 13.29 lakh new voters, including first-time voters, added. . As on October 2, a total of 11.78 lakh form 8 and 8.85 lakh form 6 applications had been received, against 84,900 form 7 applications. . “During every summary revision, 8 lakh to 10 lakh new voters, including 4 lakh to 5 lakh first-time voters, are added and another 4 lakh to 5 lakh names deleted,” the official said. . Since 2023, shifted voters need only to submit form 8 with supporting documents at their new residence, following which their names are automatically deleted from the old booth or constituency. . Officials said declarations in forms 6 to 8 also act as a deterrent against fraud. . Duplicate entries, meanwhile, will be weeded out of the final rolls using software to detect photo and demographic similarities.

briefs.headline: Hindu voters are being struck off rolls: BJP MLC C T Ravi
briefs.deck: Hindu voters are being struck off rolls: Ravi
briefs.bodyText: Chitradurga: Disputing Congress leaders’ claims that Muslim voters were selectively being removed from the electoral rolls en masse, former minister and BJP MLC C T Ravi on Saturday remarked that the situation on the ground was starkly different. “It is actually Hindu voters whose names are being deleted from the rolls. In Chikkamagaluru constituency alone, the names of 32,000 Hindus have been struck off the rolls,” Ravi told reporters in Chitradurga. . The Congress leaders have hatched a conspiracy to ensure that reports of deletion of Hindu voters do not come to light, said Ravi. “Of the 37,000 names removed from the electoral rolls in Chikkamagaluru, 32,000 are Hindus. This is nothing short of treason,” he fumed. .Mysuru: Congress leader Showkath Pasha demands all-party meet to discuss Form 7 issue. Ravi pointed out that the rules allowed people to submit objections using Form 7. “Officials must investigate these claims, and if they find that the names of certain voters are to be struck off the rolls, let them do so legally. Else, ensure that the voters’ names are included in the rolls. However, the chief minister is trying to protect the voting rights of illegal migrants,” he said.

briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Continuing his unrelenting campaign against Chief Minister D K Shivakumar over the latter's alleged role in the NICE project scam, Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy on Saturday sought to know how the CM and members of his family had managed to get their hands on land notified by the government for an infrastructure project. . Pointing to a property worth Rs 2,000 crore near the Hosakerehalli toll plaza on NICE road, Kumaraswamy asked, "Who does the Sobha apartment complex near Hosakerehalli toll plaza belong to? What is the connection between Shivakumar, his brother D K Suresh and the apartment complex? Who are Amasse Gowda, Bhagyalakshmi and Kempegowda?" .Karnataka drought: Farmers facing severe hardship, says CM DK Shivakumar. Accusing Shivakumar and his family members of forcibly acquiring land by threatening property owners, Kumaraswamy asked, "How was it possible for the CM, and his family members to purchase land notified for a project by the government?" . The Union Minister further said that he had been approached by some people, pleading him to stay silent on the NICE road scam. "I told them that I cannot be bought," said Kumaraswamy, reiterating his willingness to fight for those who lost their land to the project. "If the people remain united, I will save the project for the state," he added.

briefs.headline: Neeru Dhanda eyes Olympic medal to end wait since Rajyavardhan’s 2004 silver
briefs.deck: After battling viral fever and a rushed recovery, Neeru Dhanda arrived at the Asian Games 2026 with a dream of winning a medal. She left Aichi-Nagoya with three medals - two golds and a silver - and her sights now firmly set on the Los Angeles Olympics. With the World Championship in Doha her immediate target, Neeru wants to win an Olympic medal and end India’s long wait for a shotgun medal.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Days before leaving for the Asian Games 2026, Neeru Dhanda was hospitalised with viral fever. She had barely any time to recover before boarding the flight to Japan. There was no proper recovery period. Just medicines, ORS, and a dream of winning a medal at the Asian Games.
When she reached Aichi-Nagoya and entered her hotel room, Neeru picked up her gun and told herself three words: "Nerru, tu training pe hai (Neeru, you are in training."
It was a message she wanted to give her own mind - a way of staying focused and refusing to think about the illness.
With water bottles, ORS and medicines by her side, Neeru kept her dream alive. The trap shooter, who had won gold at the ISSF World Cup in Lonato earlier this year, eventually stepped onto the range, loaded her ammunition and shot her way to glory.
She finished the Asian Games with three medals - two golds and a silver - emerging as one of India's standout performers.
From illness to three medals
Neeru first won gold in the women's individual trap event. She then teamed up with Manisha Keer and Aashima Ahlawat to win silver in the women's trap team event. 
On the penultimate day of the shooting competition, she partnered Kynan Chenai to win gold in the trap mixed team event.
Nagoya: From left, India's Manisha Keer, Ashima Ahlawat and Neeru Dhanda pose with the national flag after winning the silver medal. (PTI Photo)
But behind the three medals was a battle that began even before she reached the shooting range.
“I didn't let my mind receive the message that I was sick or unwell. I didn't want to let myself think that I was sick. Whenever I felt down or weak, I used to tell myself loudly, ‘Neeru, tu training pe hai abhi.’ This is what kept me motivated throughout the Asian Games,” Neeru told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview.
“Honestly, I felt very weak because there was no recovery period after the hospitalisation. I thought about skipping the Games, but no, I am very stubborn. I wanted to do something different. Very few people get this opportunity. I was lucky that I got it, and I am happy that I delivered,” she said.
Gold medallist India's Neeru Dhanda, left, and Kynan Chenai (PTI Photo)
Neeru dedicated her three-medal haul to late Raja Randhir Singh, India's first Asian Games shooting gold medallist, who passed away aged 79 in May. Randhir, a five-time Olympian, had won India's first Asian Games shooting gold in 1978.
Neeru had met him a few times and remembered the encouragement he gave her.
“I dedicate these medals to late Raja Randhir Singh. He was a lovely soul. I got to meet him a couple of times. Whenever he met me, he blessed me. He always said, ‘Beta, be brave. You are a shooter, you need to be brave. Shoot with bravery, you will get the result.’ Those words helped me a lot in Aichi-Nagoya,” Neeru said.
"I also want to dedicate to my federation, SAI, SAI Bhopal, Bhopa Shooting Academy where I train, my coaches, and everyone who has been with me throughout this journey," she said.
Mission Olympics begins
The World Cup is done. The Asian Games are done. Now, Neeru has set her sights on the Los Angeles Olympics. Her immediate target is the World Championship in Doha, which will offer a quota opportunity for the 2028 Olympics.
“The moment I leave Japan, my target will shift towards the World Championship in Doha. That is a quota competition for the Los Angeles Olympics, so I will focus on that. That is my ultimate goal. Olympics mein medal jeetna hai,” she said.
India have won several Olympic medals in shooting, but the shotgun disciplines have produced only one Olympic medal for the country - Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore's silver in men's double trap at the 2004 Athens Olympics.
After her performances in Aichi-Nagoya, Neeru will be one of the Indian shooters attracting attention ahead of the Los Angeles Games.
‘Golden girl’? Neeru loves it
Neeru has also earned the nickname ‘golden girl’ after her recent run of success. Asked about the title, she laughed.
“Golden girl title... I just love it. I love this title. I hope it continues to be like this always. It was possible because of the hard work I have put in day and night,” she said.
For Neeru, the key has been constantly looking back at her own performances and learning from her mistakes.
“Introspection has always helped me. Whenever I do something wrong or make mistakes, I ask myself, ‘Where did I go wrong?’ I get that answer. That helps me a lot,” she said.
Little time with family
After returning home with three medals, Neeru was eager to meet her parents and family and celebrate her success with them.
But she had only a few hours. Neeru was at her home in Sangatpura village in Jind, speaking to her mother, when she received a call that gave her another reason to return to Japan.
Former India shooter and deputy chef de mission Anjali Bhagwat told her that she had been selected as India's women's flag bearer for the closing ceremony of the Asian Games 2026. Within hours, Neeru packed her bags and headed back to the airport.
“I got a call from Anjali Bhagwat ma'am. She asked me to be the flag bearer at the closing ceremony. It's a big honour for me. I didn't want to let it go,” Neeru told TimesofIndia.com.
Her parents were delighted by the news. “My parents are so happy. When I gave them the news about the closing ceremony, my mother said, ‘Ja beta, mauka nahi milta ye kisi ko. Aaja, phir se khushi manayenge,’” Neeru said.

stories.headline: Bengaluru turns pink in a march against patriarchy
stories.bodyText:
Over 300 women dressed in pink took to Bengaluru’s streets on October 2, demanding safer public spaces and challenging patriarchy. The all-women march began at Mahatma Gandhi Park in Shivajinagar around 8 pm and wound through Kasturba Road before ending at Freedom Park. Carrying flashlights and torches, participants lit up the stretches they walked through. Organised as part of the wider Why Loiter Campaign, the march was held in solidarity with similar women-led protests in Delhi, Mumbai, Guwahati, Panjim, Kolkata, Bhubaneswar and other cities.
As the group made its way through the poorly lit road, women could be heard remarking, “Just imagine walking through these streets alone at this hour.” Their safety concerns, which often shape how they navigate everyday life, were echoed throughout the march through chants such as “Smash patriarchy”, “Mere sar mein dard hai, iska karan mard hai”, “Ek kachori, do samosa, in mardon ka kya bharosa” and “Patriarchy hatao, desh bachao”.
The power of pink
For Janacina, pink held a personal meaning. “I believe every girl goes through a phase of hating pink because of the pressure to fit into a category. 
But later, we embrace it as a new identity. To me, it symbolises growing up as a girl,” she said. At the march, pink became a symbol of solidarity. “To me, it means love, care and unity among women,” she added.
Theatrical poet and Bengaluru march organiser Nupur Azadi said pink, or gulabi, was chosen as a nationwide call to action. “Not in an ironic way, but more in a joyous, hopeful reclamation way,” she said, adding that the idea was to reclaim both the streets and the colour itself. Some participants questioned the theme and chose to wear what they wanted.
The right to feel safe
Software engineer Ronita joined the march with her seven-year-old daughter, determined to create a safer future for her. “I don't think I had a choice. It is my duty as a woman to be here and bring her with me. She will grow up and ask me what I did to secure her future, and I should be able to answer,” she said. The mother-daughter duo carried a placard that read, ‘Am I next?’, which Ronita said reflected a question ‘lingering in all of our minds’.
For 19-year-old Janacina, feminism is about more than women’s rights; it is about equality and challenging patriarchy. She believes collective action can slowly shift mindsets. “Little by little, voice by voice, through protests, things can change, people can change, and sooner or later, the mentality of the country will change,” she shared. “I believe this protest helps guide me towards knowing myself a little more.”

stories.headline: KSRTC to install 100 ADAS systems in buses across Karnataka
stories.deck: The ADAS units will combine cameras, sensors, GPS and connectivity features to monitor both the road environment and the driver’s behaviour.
stories.bodyText:
The Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) is set to install 100 Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) in its buses to improve road safety, monitor driver behaviour and provide real-time alerts on potential hazards.
Recently, the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) also announced plans to install ADAS technology in 50 buses as part of a pilot project.
According to KSRTC officials, the systems will be deployed across the corporation’s divisions in Karnataka, with installation and commissioning expected to be carried out between November 2026 and October 2027. The systems are expected to be installed at locations covering 17 KSRTC divisions across the State.
The ADAS units will combine cameras, sensors, GPS, and connectivity features to monitor both the road environment and the driver’s behaviour. The system will include a forward-facing road camera and a driver-monitoring camera, along with other cameras and hardware required for monitoring the surroundings of the bus.
A senior KSRTC official said: “The system is designed to detect several potential road-safety risks, including forward collision risks, lane departure, pedestrians, insufficient distance from vehicles ahead and other hazardous situations. It will also provide alerts to drivers through visual, audible, and buzzer warnings.”
“The driver-monitoring component will focus on identifying signs of fatigue and distraction. It will be capable of detecting drowsiness, yawning, prolonged eye closure, mobile-phone use, driver distraction and driver absence, among other behaviours. The system is also designed to monitor certain aspects of driver posture and attention while the bus is in operation,” the official explained.
The ADAS units will have 4G LTE connectivity and GPS/NavIC support, allowing vehicle and event-related information to be transmitted for monitoring and analysis. The specifications also provide for substantial onboard storage for recorded video and event data.
KSRTC officials said that the system will be linked to a cloud-based fleet management and analytics platform. This will enable authorised personnel to monitor vehicles, review safety alerts and access relevant video footage associated with incidents or detected events. The system is expected to support the retrieval of event-related video, allowing incidents such as sudden braking, collision warnings or driver-related safety alerts to be examined. The specifications also provide for driver-behaviour analysis and reporting.
The KSRTC tender requires the selected agency to be responsible for supplying, installing, and commissioning the systems in KSRTC buses at designated locations. The corporation has also specified three years of comprehensive warranty support, along with availability of spare parts for at least 10 years.
Officials added that the deployment is expected to give KSRTC access to data on both vehicle movement and driver behaviour, potentially providing officials with a broader picture of safety-related events across the fleet.

stories.headline: Bengaluru Jatre: City to host 10-day cultural festival from December 4
stories.bodyText:
After the success of its one-of-a-kind Freedom Habba, Bengaluru will host a 10-day city-wide cultural festival — “Bengaluru Jatre” — from December 4 to 13, with the State government planning programmes across public spaces, educational institutions, museums, Namma Metro stations and other venues, Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda announced on Saturday.
The event will bring together music, theatre, literature, food, art, heritage, and other cultural activities on a common platform, the Minister said, addressing the media here.
“Government agencies are expected to organise more than 100 programmes, all of which will be free to attend,” Mr. Gowda said, adding that a central website is planned to carry the festival calendar and connect visitors with individual programmes organised by participating institutions.
Mr. Gowda said the festival is being conceived on the lines of the traditional Ooru Habba or Jatre in Karnataka, where an entire community comes together to celebrate. He added that the government would adapt the idea to Bengaluru by allowing neighbourhoods, institutions, artists, businesses, and communities to organise their own programmes. “There will be no single Jatre ground and no single central stage. Instead, Bengaluru itself will become the stage,” Mr. Gowda said.
“Unity does not mean uniformity. Bengaluru has many colours and expressions. We want every neighbourhood, institution, and community to celebrate in its own way and still feel that it is part of one Jatre,” he said, pointing out that the event is intended to complement the government’s focus on civic infrastructure. “A government that works every day to address the everyday problems faced by citizens also has a responsibility to enrich the lives of people living in an increasingly mechanical and fast-paced urban environment, while preserving and promoting the State’s rich art and cultural traditions,” he said.
The five corporations can use parks and grounds for citizen-led activities, while the Tourism Department and Karnataka State Tourism Development Corporation could use heritage sites for programmes and Bengaluru-specific experiences. Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited is expected to explore performances and busking at Metro concourses, while the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation could carry the festival’s branding across its bus network. Schools, colleges, museums, galleries, science centres, cultural institutions and corporate campuses have also been invited to participate, Mr. Gowda said.

briefs.headline: Missed voter list? Mop-up drive may give you another chance during SIR drive in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Lakhs of 
Karnataka
 voters who were left out of the draft electoral rolls may not have to wait for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to end to get back on the list. Officials are looking at starting a special mop-up drive while the exercise is still on.
The Election Commission of India (ECI) has asked states that have completed SIR to run such a drive to enrol left-out voters. Karnataka, where SIR is still under way, is keen to start early.
The state has 1.08 crore voters missing from the draft list published on Aug 24, and a significant number of them have shifted or are absent. The only way to reverse a deletion during the claims, objections and notice phase was to apply through Form 6. Those who applied before Sept 23 had a chance of making it to the final rolls. But only a little over 7 lakh people applied through Form 6 and Form 6A (for NRI voters), so many remain out.
“With most of the groundwork completed, a majority of the 60,923 BLOs are free and they will start the mop-up drive,” chief electoral officer V Anbu Kumar told 
TOI
.
Kumar said a meeting, including one with political parties, has been called on Monday and more clarity would emerge then. 
He added that there was no question of one waiting once ECI guidelines are issued.
Sham, a volunteer from KR Pura who has coordinated with BLOs, EROs and voters during SIR, said BLOs are expected to begin early next week by handing out Form 6 to voters on the ASDDO list. “Those BLOs who find it hard to enrol voters through this process are allowed to take other BLOs’ help for the same,” he said. However, BLOs and EROs from RT Nagar, Whitefield and Chikpete said they were unaware of any rollout, though they had heard about the ECI guidelines.
In its Oct 1 instruction, ECI reiterated that enrolment was a continuous process, and anyone not yet enrolled or whose name was deleted could apply at any time. “The objective of the special drive is to identify and facilitate such electors.”
Political parties will get the list of names being added through Form 6, and the final list once the exercise ends, so that left-out voters can be enrolled.
As of Friday, the state had completed 35.6 lakh hearings out of 43.8 lakh notices. It has set itself an Oct 12 deadline to finish the notices phase, ahead of ECI’s Oct 22 cut-off.

briefs.headline: Drought-hit Karnataka seeks Rs 7,142 crore from Centre
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 With 217 of 
Karnataka
’s 240 taluks declared drought-hit, chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 Saturday sought Rs 7,142 crore from the Centre, saying farmers were facing crop losses, water shortage and severe distress.
Shivakumar made the appeal at a meeting with the Centre’s inter-ministerial drought assessment team, headed by Ajit Kumar Sahu, joint secretary in the Union agriculture and farmers welfare ministry. The team is on a three-day visit to assess crop losses and verify the state govt’s estimates.
“Karnataka is facing a severe drought situation, and farmers and other people are facing great hardship. Provide Rs 7,142 crore in drought relief to the state as per National Disaster Response Force norms,” Shivakumar urged the team.
Govt briefed the team on rainfall deficit, crop losses, drinking water shortage, and fodder availability. Shivakumar said relief was needed to prevent further strain on the rural economy. “If farmers are pushed into distress, the entire system comes to a standstill. Therefore, the central govt must come forward to support the farmers of Karnataka,” he said.
“We’ve never seen people suffer to this extent. This is an extremely distressing situation. 
A special session was convened to understand the problems faced by people’s representatives and farmers, and 150 MLAs raised issues concerning their constituencies,” Shivakumar said, adding that reservoir inflows remained low except in the Krishna basin, while Malnad and coastal Karnataka were facing severe rainfall deficit. Urban areas, too, were reporting water shortages.
“Despite this, Cauvery Water Management Authority is directing the release of water into Cauvery river. The state govt has announced Rs 2,500 in relief for farmers, but we are expecting greater assistance from the Centre,” he said.
Many sections hit
Govt also highlighted pressure on different sections of the rural economy. “Farmers are facing severe hardship. Sugarcane growers are demanding higher prices, while milk producers are seeking an increase of at least Rs 10 in milk prices. In this challenging situation, let the Centre and state work together,” the CM added.
Three central teams are assessing the situation in the Tumakuru-Chitradurga-Davanagere belt, North Karnataka, and Mysuru region. They will meet deputy commissioners and local officials and verify data submitted by the state. Sahu assured Shivakumar that the teams would assess the situation on the ground, collect data and submit an objective report.
The state has already submitted two memoranda seeking drought assistance. The second, covering 177 taluks, estimated losses at around Rs 46,000 crore. Govt has put the overall damage at Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 60,000 crore. A final memorandum covering all 217 drought-hit taluks will be submitted after the central teams complete their assessment.
Kharge to PM: 31 lakh families need help now
More than 31 lakh farming families in Karnataka are battling crop losses, prompting Congress president 
Mallikarjun Kharge
 to seek urgent central assistance.
In an 11-page letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, also shared with home minister Amit Shah, Kharge made six requests, including quick assessment and compensation for small and marginal farmers. Sharing the letter on X, the Rajya Sabha LoP sought Modi’s personal intervention.
“The state is facing one of its gravest drought situations in recent years, with a 58% rainfall deficiency as of Sept, widespread crop losses, and severe distress for lakhs of farming families,” he said.
Kharge also sought input subsidies based on Karnataka’s updated Bhoomi land records instead of the outdated 2015-16 agriculture census, to ensure no eligible farmer is excluded.

briefs.headline: Banks must act with due care over loan default: Karnataka high court
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A bank or a financial institution should act responsibly while invoking criminal processes against a customer, Karnataka high court observed in a recent judgement, giving relief to a homebuyer in a loan case.
An outstanding loan cannot be a ground to start criminal proceedings, which cannot be reduced to a tool to recover money, Justice Suraj Govindaraj noted in the order passed on Sept 25.
Pritesh Bari, from Bengaluru, was a signatory to the tripartite agreement involving the purchase of an apartment. According to SBI’s complaint, the builder had sold the property without the bank’s consent even though the Rs 40 lakh loan had not been paid by the petitioner or the developers/partners.
SBI claimed Pritesh had said a registered sale deed would be executed in his favour, but he became irregular in servicing the loan.
On the other hand, Pritesh claimed that as per the agreement, in the event of the builder cancelling the booking on account of loan default or project delay, then the builder would pay the amount received from the borrower to the bank.
The agreement stipulated that the builder would not transfer the apartment to other buyers without the bank’s written consent.
Justice Govindaraj noted the project was admittedly not completed, no sale deed was executed in favour of the petitioner and the property was subsequently sold to a third party.
If the bank was aggrieved by the builder or by failure to honour the tripartite agreement, the same could have been pursued against the persons responsible in accordance with law. The bank, however, has proceeded against the petitioner merely because the loan account had not been cleared.
The bank’s action is “wholly unwarranted” and deserves to be deprecated, the court said.

briefs.headline: Fireball explosion leaves 6 of family injured in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Six members of a family, including four children, suffered serious burn injuries after a fireball explosion due to the leakage of liquefied petroleum gas from a domestic cylinder at their rented house in Vinayaka Layout, Nayandahalli, in west Bengaluru, in the early hours of Friday.
Based on the primary investigation, police said the incident occurred between 6.30am and 7am, when the gas reportedly leaked from the cylinder as the stove was being lit and suddenly caught fire, engulfing the house and injuring Karilingappa, 40, his wife Lakshmamma, 43, and their four children — 11-year-old Chaitra, nine-year-old Basava, and three-year-old twins Geetha and Girija.
The force of the explosion sent household articles flying across the room, while the loud explosion jolted neighbours awake. On rushing to the spot, neighbours found the house engulfed in flames. They pulled the injured out and helped rush all six to the burns ward at Victoria Hospital.
On receiving information about the incident, Chandra Layout police and fire and emergency personnel reached the spot and doused the fire.
The family was living in a house measuring 10x10 square feet, with a hall and small kitchen covered by an asphaltic sheet roof. Lakshmamma went to light the stove carrying one of the twins. Since the gas had leaked overnight, the explosion occurred. Karilingappa and the three other children were still sleeping in the hall.
Lakshmamma has reportedly suffered burns over 70% of her body, while Karilingappa sustained around 45% burns. The condition of Lakshmamma and the four children is said to be critical.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru family loses Rs 22 lakh to fake PU board official
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A family allegedly lost Rs 22 lakh after a man claiming to be a PU department employee promised to secure an MBBS seat for their elder daughter, only to go incommunicado after collecting the money.
Anitha BM, 45, a homemaker, said her family was outside the PU department office in Malleswaram in the first week of Feb when a man overheard their conversation about their daughter’s plans to pursue medicine after appearing for NEET in 2025.
The man introduced himself as Chandrashekhar and claimed to work at PU board. He reportedly told the family he could arrange an MBBS seat at a prestigious college for Rs 22 lakh. Having gained the family’s confidence by speaking knowledgeably about NEET, Chandrashekhar later met them near a fuel station on Tumakuru Road.
The family handed over Rs 4 lakh and their daughter’s documents on Feb 11, followed by Rs 13 lakh on Feb 20. Two days later, Chandrashekhar collected another Rs 5 lakh, claiming the seat had been confirmed. The entire Rs 22 lakh was paid in cash in 2025, Anitha claimed.
A few days later, the family tried contacting him, but his phone was switched off. When they approached PU department to verify his credentials, they learnt no person by that name worked there.

briefs.headline: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar plans regional cultural showcase in Dasara procession
briefs.deck: The Dasara finale may feature tableaux from neighbouring States; Defence Ministry requested to consider an air show in Mysuru
briefs.bodyText:
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said tableaux from neighbouring States may participate in the Mysuru Dasara procession this year, with the respective State governments being requested to showcase their culture and traditions.
Speaking to reporters on Saturday, ahead of the Praja Seva campaign at Periyapatna, Mr. Shivakumar said the initiative was aimed at bringing changes to the way Dasara was organised.
“Our water goes to neighbouring States, people from neighbouring States come to our State, and our vegetables are supplied to these States. When this is the case, let the neighbouring States also participate in Dasara by bringing their tableaux and showcasing their culture,” he said.
Mr. Shivakumar said he had requested the Chief Ministers of the southern States to attend the Mysuru Dasara festivities and was in touch with them to confirm their participation.
Air show
Expressing confidence that an air show would be held during the Dasara, the Chief Minister said he had requested the Defence Minister to consider the State government’s proposal.
He said the Defence Ministry had also been requested to send personnel from the armed forces to participate in the Dasara procession. Their participation, he said, would motivate youngsters and help inculcate discipline among them.
Mr. Shivakumar said he had instructed officials to provide an opportunity to Tibetans settled in Bylakuppe near Periyapatna to present a cultural performance during Dasara.
He said that film stars, including upcoming actors and actresses, would participate in the Dasara procession. The Kannada film industry would be represented during the festivities, he added, noting that the Chamber of Commerce had agreed to support the initiative.
Drought situation

A Central team had arrived in Karnataka to assess the situation, and three teams would tour different parts of the State, he said. “I have spoken to the Central team and requested them to tour the State in detail,” he added.

briefs.headline: Engineers are architects of country’s future: Karnataka Minister N. Chaluvarayaswamy
briefs.deck: ‘Use technology for social good; Innovation, technology key to building sustainable Karnataka’

Water Resources Minister N. Chaluvarayaswamy said engineers are not merely builders of roads and buildings but architects of the country’s future.

He said the world was changing rapidly, with artificial intelligence, robotics, semiconductors, green energy, electric vehicles, and space technology transforming the way people lived. “Karnataka had a leading role to play in this technological transformation,” he said.

The responsibility of empowering these aspirations with modern technology rests with all stakeholders. Development is not limited to mega projects. Ensuring timely water supply to farmers, providing quality digital education to students, improving rural road connectivity, and creating skill-based employment opportunities for youth were also important indicators of real progress,” he said.
Technology should not merely be “smart” but also sustainable, the Minister said, urging youngsters not just to seek jobs but also to become job creators.
Recalling the contribution of Sir M. Visvesvaraya, the Minister said his vision and efficiency continue to inspire generations. Despite the limited technology available during his time, the projects he conceived and executed remain exemplary.

CIVDB chairperson P. Suryaprakash, office-bearers Sitaram, Nagaraj, H.S. Suresh Babu and Nanjayya, retired chief engineer Mahadev, and former All India Institution of Engineers president V.B. Singh were among those present.

briefs.headline: Stop filing FIRs against BJP leaders; review those filed over Form 7 applications, former CM B.S. Yediyurappa urges Karnataka DG&IGP
briefs.deck: In a memorandum, the BJP alleged that criminal cases were being registered against its party workers and political activists for submitting Form 7 objections, and claimed that the police machinery was being subjected to political pressure

A BJP delegation led by former Karnataka chief minister B.S. Yediyurappa, State unit president B.Y. Vijayendra, Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok and Leader of Opposition in the Council Chalavadi Narayanaswamy met the Director General and Inspector General of Police on October 3, urging him to ensure that FIRs registered in connection with Form 7 applications during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls be dealt with strictly according to the law.

Statutory mechanism

It argued that the mere filing of multiple or bulk Form 7 applications cannot, by itself, constitute a criminal offence.
The delegation referred to FIRs reportedly registered in Bhalki in Bidar, Belagavi and Narasimharaja in Mysuru, involving provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. It said any criminal liability must be established on the basis of evidence showing individual involvement, including whether an applicant knowingly furnished false information or forged documents.
The BJP also cited provisions in the SIR guidelines and the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023, claiming that there is no prescribed limit on the number of Form 7 applications that can be submitted and that objections are subject to verification by election officials.
The delegation further raised concern over the alleged circulation of Form 7 applications containing applicants’ names, mobile numbers and signatures on social media, and sought an inquiry into the source of the disclosure.
The BJP urged the DGP to ensure that police action remains politically neutral and that any genuine violations are proceeded against strictly according to law and due process.
Warning by Leader of Opposition

stories.headline: Hydro generation falls short, strains power supply during non-solar hours in Sept
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Hydropower generation fell nearly 12% below the projected requirement in the first six months of FY27 due to the El Nino-induced rain deficit, putting greater pressure on coal-fired generation and leading to shortages, especially during non-solar hours, in several parts of the country.
The month also saw peak power demand reach 269 GW, second only to the record 270.8 GW in May this year. There were several days during the month when peak demand crossed 250 GW - the previous peak recorded in May 2024, before demand records tumbled in May this year.
The deficit was more pronounced in Sept, when demand was unusually high due to strong industrial requirements, besides cooling and irrigation needs amid a deficient monsoon. Power ministry data showed that India faced a shortage of nearly 560 million units (MU) of electricity during the month due to lower hydropower generation and the lack of battery storage to store solar energy produced during the day for use in the evening when demand surges. For perspective, electricity shortage in Aug was around 98 MU.
While hydropower remained in deficit, coal-fired generation provided the baseload during the first half of the 2026-27 financial year. 
Though available in limited capacity, nuclear power also helped meet the load by generating more electricity than projected, while gas-based plants also came to the rescue in Sept. Power generation from renewables - solar and wind - increased 25% during the month, but their share in overall generation dropped to about 17% from 19.5% in Aug. Data showed that the overall shortage during the first six months of the financial year remained low at around 0.2% of electricity demand.
Charith Konda, lead energy specialist at Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis, said the power shortage observed so far this fiscal was largely due to lower hydropower output following a 13% rainfall deficit during the monsoon. “Usually this is the period when hydropower supports the supply. We had good rains last year and hence good hydropower generation. But it’s like one piece in the overall system; if you pull it out, all deficiencies come out,” Konda said.
“When hydropower generation falls, there is more stress on coal power and there are shortages,” he added.
Hydropower plays a crucial role in meeting evening peak demand when solar output drops. The rainfall deficit, however, changed that equation.
While coal was burnt faster due to high demand, intense rains in coal-producing states caused logistical problems in transporting supplies, leading to fuel shortages at many plants.
Konda also observed that distribution was a problem in several states, requiring macro-level thinking to strengthen the distribution network. “It is because of poor infrastructure that there is instability in the distribution grid and power cuts,” he said.
Disha Aggarwal, fellow at Council on Energy, Environment and Water, also said discoms faced real constraints, from stressed finances to subsidy pressures, requiring smarter planning. “Yet our power system still runs on older assumptions about weather and demand. India needs a heat-resilient, flexible grid, and three shifts can get us there. First, strengthen supply during non-solar hours through storage, complementary wind and flexible coal. Second, help consumers shift demand to periods of abundant supply by scaling smart metering and time-of-day tariffs. And third, discoms must plan locally for heat risk by using AI to combine feeder, transformer and meter data with local weather forecasts, so they can spot demand hotspots before networks see outages and transformers fail,” Aggarwal said.
Amit Manohar, secretary general of Indian Solar Manufacturers Association, said faster rollout of solar-plus-storage projects and stronger networks was required to ensure reliable power at all hours. “Solar now meets a large share of daytime electricity requirement, helping the grid manage peak demand without shortages. The challenge comes after sunset. Pairing solar with storage will help close this gap,” Manohar said.
Rohit Bajaj, joint managing director of Indian Energy Exchange, said the power ministry was closely monitoring the coal situation at power plants and had taken steps to ensure fuel availability. “Demand and supply dynamics remained volatile during the month, particularly in the last week, as cyclone activity and widespread rainfall moderated demand across several regions,” Bajaj said.

stories.headline: Third edition of Green Energy Corridor to add 51,126 ckm transmission lines, 50 GWh BESS
stories.deck: The Indian government has approved the third phase of the Green Energy Corridor to enhance renewable energy transmission. This phase will create over 51,000 circuit kilometres of transmission lines and significant transformation capacity. It also includes the installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems to store excess renewable energy. The implementation involves a mix of new projects and…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The rapid growth in solar and wind power generation, along with rising grid congestion and renewable energy curtailment, has prompted govt to announce a new transmission scheme with the launch of the third phase of the Green Energy Corridor (GEC), which got the Cabinet’s nod on Wednesday.
With an outlay of nearly Rs 1.9 lakh crore, GEC-III will strengthen intra-state transmission networks by creating 51,126 circuit kilometres of transmission lines and nearly 229 GVA of transformation capacity to evacuate 135 GW of renewable energy across states and Union territories. The infrastructure will facilitate the transfer of electricity from generating units to the grid and eventually to consumers.
GEC is a govt programme to set up dedicated transmission infrastructure to integrate large-scale renewable energy into the national power grid.
The scheme also includes deployment of 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), which will help store surplus green energy, provide grid flexibility and meet demand during non-solar hours.
The scheme’s outlay of Rs 1,86,405 crore comprises Rs 1,36,378 crore for developing intra-state transmission systems and Rs 50,000 crore for BESS over seven years. 
It involves total central financial support of Rs 54,082 crore, which will help offset intra-state transmission charges and keep power costs down.
Curtailment of renewable energy has emerged as a major challenge due to inadequate transmission networks. More than 8,000 GWh of RE was curtailed in Q1 of 2026-27. GEC-III is expected to address the problem to some extent.
Santosh Kumar Sarangi, secretary, ministry of new and renewable energy, said 70% of the scheme would comprise greenfield or new projects, which will be awarded through tariff-based competitive bidding, with transmission service providers building, owning, operating and maintaining the assets. The remaining 30% will comprise brownfield upgrades and network strengthening works, which will be executed on a cost-plus basis, under which the project cost and approved return will be recovered through regulated tariffs. State transmission utilities will be the overall implementing agencies.
Sarangi said the last project under GEC-I was expected to be completed by the end of the ongoing financial year, while all projects under GEC-II were likely to be completed by March 2028.
To ensure the projects adhere to timelines, Sarangi said a project monitoring committee headed by a joint secretary will regularly review their progress, while he will review them every three months. “There is going to be a steering committee at the level of cabinet secretary, which will monitor the progress of this scheme every six months,” he said. The remaining projects under GEC-II will also be monitored by the steering committee.
The ministry has also tied BESS deployment to domestic content requirements (DCR) to spur local manufacturing in the sector. Sarangi said technical consultations will be held to frame guidelines for DCR for locally made components.

stories.headline: RBI chief lays down 5 key priorities to maintain financial stability amidst emerging risks
stories.deck: “Financial instability anywhere can become a threat to financial stability everywhere”.
stories.bodyText:
As multiple shocks threaten financial stability Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Saturday emphasised the importance of maintaining it at all costs.
Financial instability anywhere can become a threat to financial stability everywhere, he pointed out.
The challenge before financial sector regulators is to build a financial system that can withstand the shocks they anticipate and those, they cannot yet foresee, said Sanjay Malhotra, Governor, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) while laying down five key priorities that policymakers must factor in when safeguarding financial stability.
“This requires resilient institutions, better data, deeper markets, credible safety nets, effective resolution mechanisms and regulation and supervision that are proactive and forward-looking, while being proportionate,” he said in his special address at the Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave, on the topic “Preserving Financial Stability in an Evolving World”.
Firstly, stating that some shocks will be inevitable, he said financial stability was not about preventing them, it’s about strengthening systemic resilience to face those shocks and contain their amplification.
“Shocks may be endogenous or exogenous. Our aim must be to foster a financial system that can provide financial services in all states of the world, even under severe shocks,” he said.
Secondly, as a new generation of systemic risks were taking shape, he said assessing them and their complex interactions was vital.
“Risks are increasingly exogenous, cross-border and interconnected. The next financial crisis may not originate in a bank, or even in finance. It may begin with a geopolitical event, a cyberattack, or a technological failure and affect the financial system through multiple channels,” he cautioned.
To strengthen systemic resilience, those responsible must aim to better understand the network of dependencies and contagion channels and make scenario analysis a cornerstone of risk management.
Thirdly, monitoring and assessment frameworks must improve. “For that, we need better and more granular data. The financial system is becoming increasingly complex, but data on NBFIs, interconnected exposures, technology dependencies and cross-border positions remain fragmented,” the Governor said.
In an increasingly interconnected financial system, the quality of our data would increasingly determine the quality of our risk assessment, he stated.
Fourthly he said, resilience must be system-wide. “A strong banking system is necessary, but not sufficient. We need resilience across sectors and institutions: NBFIs, financial markets, payment systems, technology infrastructure, critical third parties and cross-border financial networks,” he emphasised.
“Financial instability anywhere can become a threat to financial stability everywhere,” he pointed out. Fifth, he said, innovation must strengthen, not fragment, the foundations of trust.
“Artificial intelligence, tokenisation, and new forms of financial intermediation can dramatically improve efficiency. But innovation will be sustainable only if the financial system preserves the fundamental properties on which trust rests: sound institutions, settlement finality, singleness of money, and financial integrity,” Mr Malhotra stated.
“If we succeed, financial stability will remain largely invisible. And, in central banking, invisibility is perhaps the most meaningful measure of success,” he highlighted.

briefs.headline: Bulk diesel price up Rs 14.6/litre as crude surge squeezes oil cos' margins
briefs.deck: Nayara raises petrol price by Rs 5/litre, diesel by Rs 3 as crude surge hits margins
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Oil marketing companies have increased the price of bulk diesel by Rs 14.6 per litre, while private retailer Nayara Energy has raised pump prices of petrol and diesel by Rs 5 and Rs 3 per litre respectively, as elevated crude prices have started hurting their margins.
Nayara Energy now sells petrol at Rs 108 a litre in Haryana, while diesel is priced at Rs 98.84. Fuel prices vary between states due to differences in tax structures. Nayara Energy operates 7,108 petrol pumps across India.
Bulk diesel, used by commercial, industrial and institutional customers, is now priced at Rs 153.57 per litre, up from Rs 138.97 in Sept. The price of bulk diesel reflects the actual market price of the fuel and is aligned directly with international product benchmarks. In contrast, the price of diesel and petrol for automobiles sold at retail outlets run by public sector oil marketing companies is regulated by govt and currently frozen at Rs 95.64 and Rs 102.12 a litre, respectively, in the capital.
Global benchmark Brent traded at $102.25-a-barrel on Friday for Dec contracts, Indian basket of crude, last updated on Sept 30, was priced at $117.28 per barrel.
Petroleum dealers said the substantial price difference of Rs 57.93 per litre between retail and bulk diesel has already prompted some commercial and industrial customers to buy their supplies from retail outlets. 
“There is a spike in our sales of diesel since the price of bulk diesel was revised. But we don’t have a means to differentiate commercial and industrial buyers from retail customers. The more diesel we sell, the more losses oil companies will incur,” said Monty Sehgal, spokesperson for the Federation of All India Petroleum Association.
While there are reports of private retailers rationing diesel sales to customers following increased buying by commercial users to keep their losses in check, PSU retailers said they cannot take such decisions. An executive of an oil marketing company said any surge in sales through retail outlets would be known only in a week or 10 days.
Following directions from govt, state-run oil retailers had introduced a cap of 200 litres per customer during the West Asia war, when crude supplies were disrupted, prices had surged and industrial and commercial customers started buying from retail outlets because of the price difference. The cap was subsequently removed.

briefs.headline: How landlord won tax relief on Rs 14.96 lakh demonetisation cash deposit
briefs.deck: The Bangalore bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) recently held that rental income already disclosed to the income tax authorities can be considered as an identifiable source of cash deposited into a bank account at a later date. Even where a landlord claims to have collected rent in cash, the subsequent deposit of that money cannot be disregarded merely because the rental earnings…
briefs.bodyText:
When it comes to income and taxation, documents and money trail form an important part of the process. This is particularly important when income from any of your sources is in cash. In one such case, a landlord faced income tax scrutiny due to cash deposits made on account of rental income that he received.
The Bangalore bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) recently held that rental income already disclosed to the income tax authorities can be considered as an identifiable source of cash deposited into a bank account at a later date.
Even where a landlord claims to have collected rent in cash, the subsequent deposit of that money cannot be disregarded merely because the rental earnings have already been taxed.
In this case, the tribunal clarified that disclosed rental receipts must be considered while examining the taxpayer's cash flow.
What the case is about
A man in Bengaluru owned properties that he rented out and collected the rent in cash. He also received substantial amounts as rental advances, but again in cash. During 
demonetisation
, when Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes ceased to be legal tender, the landlord in this case deposited Rs 14.96 lakh in cash into his bank account.
The man had income from three sources: salary, house property and other sources. Between November 9 and December 30, 2016, he deposited as much as Rs 14.96 lakh into his bank account. This prompted the 
Income Tax Department
 to select his return for scrutiny to establish the source of the cash.
The Assessing Officer (AO) at Koramangala subsequently issued a tax notice requiring him to explain where the deposited cash had come from.
The man on his part submitted that the deposits were on account of the money that he had accumulated over a period from income sources already disclosed to the department.
His cash position included an opening balance of Rs 10,05,793 on April 1, 2016, in addition to rental income, advances received from tenants, bank withdrawals and other receipts during the financial year.
He supported his explanation with cash books, bank statements, cash-flow statements, financial statements and records showing how the cash moved over time. The AO remained unconvinced and classified the entire deposit of Rs 14,96,500 as 'unexplained money' under Section 69A.
The tax officer rejected the man’s explanation, following which he challenged the decision before the Bangalore ITAT.
The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), or CIT(A) also sustained the addition.
The concerns underlying the decision included the substantial cash balance claimed by the man, his comparatively modest household withdrawals and certain receipts recorded shortly before demonetisation.
The landlord ultimately succeeded before the tribunal in August 2026.
How did the landlord win the case?
The ITAT Bangalore ordered the deletion of the entire addition of Rs 14,96,500 made under Section 69A. With that addition removed, the issue of applying Section 115BBE to the amount also became irrelevant. The man’s appeal was accordingly allowed.
Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that the man faced an 'unexplained cash' notice under Section 69A after the AO refused to accept his explanation for the cash deposited during demonetisation.
The Bangalore ITAT took a different view after examining the records. It found that the man had established a continuous trail demonstrating the availability of cash.
His cash-flow statement reflected an opening balance of Rs 4.72 lakh as of April 1, 2015, followed by cash received through rent, bank withdrawals and other disclosed sources. These transactions resulted in a cash balance of Rs 10.05 lakh on April 1, 2016. Additional cash inflows were also documented for the period from April to October 2016, according to the ET report.
Surana says: “Thus, the explanation was not based on a sudden cash entry immediately before demonetisation but on a running cash-flow extending from the preceding financial year.”
Surana said one of the key considerations in the man’s favour was that the Assessing Officer had based the assessment on a mistaken assumption that the cash deposits arose from business transactions or “cash sales”.
The man had never stated that he was engaged in such a business. His explanation throughout was that the money had accumulated from rental collections, advances received from tenants, bank withdrawals and other sources already disclosed to the tax authorities.
The ITAT Bangalore, therefore, found that rejecting his explanation because he could not establish cash sales or produce business books did not deal with the actual source of funds he had put forward.
