5k+ users already voted today 
Surana said the tribunal also disagreed with the argument that rental earnings could not be treated as a source for the bank deposits simply because they had already been taxed under the head “Income from House Property”.
Significance of what ITAT said
The ITAT clarified that whether a receipt is taxable and whether it can explain the availability of cash are two distinct issues. Where rent declared to the tax authorities was genuinely collected in cash, those receipts could subsequently be deposited into a bank account.
Surana says: “Similarly, there was no statutory requirement requiring an individual to immediately deposit cash receipts into a bank merely because the Income Tax Department considered the amount retained in cash to be high.”
In other words, suspicion over the amount of cash accumulated by a taxpayer cannot, by itself, justify an addition.
Surana said that when a taxpayer identifies the source of funds and submits a cash-flow statement along with supporting documents, the department must assess the material objectively. It must also produce affirmative evidence to establish why the taxpayer's explanation is incorrect.
In this matter, there was no evidence to establish that the cash-flow statement was fabricated, that the declared rental receipts had not actually been collected, that the rental advances were fictitious or that the cash available with him had already been utilised for other purposes.
Surana said the ITAT Bangalore consequently held that the man’s explanation could not be discarded simply because the tax authorities regarded his accumulated cash balance as unusually large.
The taxpayer succeeded because he demonstrated a credible and consistent trail explaining both the origin of the money and its continued availability. In contrast, the department's decision to reject his explanation rested largely on doubts and assumptions, without evidence contradicting the records he had submitted.

briefs.headline: Titan Company deepens focus on mechanical horology as category grows almost 5-fold
briefs.deck: Newly launched platform Vetra will allow Titan to progressively develop capabilities across different mechanical functions and propositions, including open-heart constructions, GMT and date complications to cater to growing consumer appreciation for craftsmanship and engineering: Titan Watches CEO (pic shared)
briefs.bodyText:
Mechanical watchmaking is entering an important phase in India, driven by a growing consumer appreciation for craftsmanship, engineering and the experience of owning a watch with a mechanical heart, said Kuruvilla Markose, CEO, Watches at Titan Company Ltd.
The context: India, also global markets, is undergoing a massive structural shift away from mass-market quartz watches to premium mechanical and automatic watches. Although, quartz still dominates the overall sales volumes because of its affordability, consumer interest for deeply designed wares, fast-pace of growth and value are heavily tilting toward mechanical horology, as watches have emerged to fashion or lifestyle statements from just being from a mere time-showing devices. A quartz watch is an electronic device powered by a battery, whereas a mechanical watch is a micro-engine powered by a tightly wound spring.
“We have seen the category gain significant momentum, with Titan’s mechanical watch business growing nearly fivefold over the last three years,’’ Mr. Markose told The Hindu.
Titan is expecting the segment to grow from around ₹270 crore last year to approximately ₹350 crore end of the current fiscal. “The broader opportunity is also being shaped by premiumisation, with watches above ₹25,000 growing at a significantly faster pace than the overall market,’’ he added.
To add momentum to growth of this rapidly expanding segment, Titan Company is making a strategic push into premium mechanical watchmaking by designing and branding its own in-house movement, Vetra. It embodies Titan’s philosophy of elegant ingenuity anchored in solving the most demanding challenges with clarity, precision and purpose, bringing artistry and mechanics into a single, cohesive whole. This bold venture allows the company to develop advanced precision engineering capabilities while significantly strengthening its presence in the competitive global horology market.
According to Mr. Markose, Vetra is Titan’s branded in-house automatic movement platform, built around the 7A architecture, which provides a common mechanical foundation from which the company can develop different watch propositions and complications. ``Having greater ownership of the movement gives our engineering and design teams more flexibility to develop the movement and the watch together, rather than designing around the limitations of an externally sourced catalogue movement,’’ he explained adding, this allowed Titan to progressively develop capabilities across different mechanical functions and propositions, including open-heart constructions, GMT and date complications.
He further said, Titan Automatics was the consumer expression of this capability, bringing together different applications of the Vetra platform. The collection includes the Infinium, which uses the Vetra 7A20+ movement with a 72-hour power reserve, alongside other propositions such as Dualis, Midnite and Atrium. “The move from our earlier 7000-series mechanical platforms, which generally offered around 36 to 40 hours of running time, to a 72-hour power reserve represents a meaningful step in our mechanical movement capability,’’ he claimed. The longer reserve has involved optimisation of how energy was stored and delivered within the movement, including the barrel and mainspring arrangement, he explained.
Every Vetra movement was assembled by hand and individually tested, and Titan was continuing to deepen its capabilities across this value chain. Movement R&D, precision component manufacturing, tooling, assembly and validation all need to come together to produce sophisticated mechanical movements consistently and at scale. ``Our larger ambition is to create watches that are imagined in India, engineered in India and built with the capabilities to engage consumers around the world. Vetra and Titan Automatics were an important part of that journey, as the company continued to build the engineering and manufacturing depth that could help India establish a stronger presence in modern horology, Mr. Markose further said.
The new collection of watches, designed on Vetra platform, were expected to offer watch connoisseurs and enthusiasts an experience of a new expression of Titan’s mechanical watchmaking, where the craft of the movement would be as much a part of the experience as the watch itself, said the Bengaluru-based watch manufacturer.
Earlier, officially announcing Vetra, Rahul Shukla, Vice-President and Chief Sales & Marketing Officer- Watches Division at Titan Company said, “Vetra firmly places Titan within a relatively small global community of watchmakers building in-house mechanical capabilities, while contributing to the emergence of a stronger indigenous horological ecosystem in India.’’
More importantly, it marked a significant stride in strengthening the country’s position in modern horology, Mr. Shukla added.
Other Titan Company officials at a factory-visit (Hosur) organised for the media fraternity recently said: For more than four decades, Titan, has pursued watchmaking with an ambition that extends well beyond the dial. Each milestone has brought greater depth in craft, engineering and innovation, evolving beyond the creation of timepieces to forge a distinct horological identity as much for the brand as for India’s emerging watchmaking stature.

briefs.headline: CBI files charge sheet against RCom, others in ₹3,750 crore LIC fraud case
briefs.deck: The four accused have been charged for offences of criminal conspiracy, cheating, and criminal breach of trust under the erstwhile Indian Penal Code, along with offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act
briefs.bodyText:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has filed a charge sheet against Reliance Communications Limited (RCom), two former executives of the Reliance (Anil Ambani) Group, and others in the LIC investment fraud case that caused alleged loss of ₹3,750 crore.
The agency identified the former executives as Amitabh Jhunjhunwala, the group managing director; and Vishwas Joshi, senior vice-president of Reliance Capital Limited. P. Venugopal, the then chief investment officer of LIC, has also been named.
“The four accused have been chargesheeted for offences of criminal conspiracy, cheating, and criminal breach of trust under the (erstwhile) Indian Penal Code, along with offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act. Further investigation is continuing to ascertain the role of other accused persons and to investigate other allegations,” the CBI alleged.
According to the agency, LIC subscribed to Non-Convertible Debentures (NCDs) worth ₹1,500 crore issued by RCom in 2012 on the basis of serious misrepresentations. The funds received through the NCD subscription were thereafter diverted to Group companies, thereby causing wrongful loss to LIC and corresponding wrongful gain to the accused persons and entities.
The CBI had registered the case on April 1, 2026, based on a complaint received from the LIC. The alleged loss caused amounted to ₹3,750 crore.
The agency has registered nine first information reports (FIRs) against RCom, Reliance Home Finance Limited, Reliance Commercial Finance Limited, Reliance Telecom Limited, and other Group entities, following complaints received from various public sector banks, LIC, and the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). It had earlier filed seven charge sheets in various cases.
“The investigation in these cases is being monitored by the Supreme Court. The CBI remains committed to conducting an expeditious and comprehensive investigation into these cases,” it said.

briefs.headline: SEBI examining position limits for non-agri contracts to boost liquidity
briefs.deck: The regulator is also working to reduce structural friction in commodity markets, including engaging with stakeholders on GST-related issues affecting participants who give or receive commodities through exchange platforms
briefs.bodyText:
Market regulator SEBI is examining position limits for non-agricultural contracts to improve liquidity and depth without weakening risk controls, its chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Saturday (October 3, 2026).
Speaking about reforms in the commodity derivatives market, Mr. Pandey said the market design should allow contracts to gain scale. In some agricultural commodities, physical settlement from the outset can impede market development, and a phased approach could allow contracts to mature before physical settlement becomes mandatory.
He said SEBI has completed consultations on the matter and guidelines will follow.
The regulator is also working to reduce structural friction in commodity markets, including engaging with stakeholders on GST-related issues affecting participants who give or receive commodities through exchange platforms.
Mr. Pandey said technology should serve the specific needs of commodity markets, which include producers, commercial users, farmers, processors, and physical hedgers.
"Technology can improve access and efficiency, but its design must reflect their needs while preserving fair access and market integrity," he said at an event organised by CPAI (Commodity & Capital Market Participants Association of India).
On investor awareness, Mr. Pandey said SEBI will strengthen efforts under Project Jagrook to spread awareness about commodity derivatives among farmers, farmer producer organisations (FPOs), MSMEs, hedgers and other market users.
"Access without understanding is not inclusion," he said, stressing the need for participants to understand both the utility and risks associated with commodity derivatives.
SEBI is also working towards deeper and more liquid cash markets, with wider participation, stronger securities borrowing and lending, and efficient hedging and arbitrage expected to improve price discovery and strengthen the interaction between cash and derivatives markets.
Mr. Pandey said simpler regulation should not mean weaker compliance, and robust controls over client funds, margins, reporting and supervision remain fundamental.
"Trust and market integrity" must not be compromised, he added.
Last month, the SEBI board approved a proposal to allow foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to participate in physically settled, non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts, subject to safeguards.

briefs.headline: Rate hike may hurt select NBFC segments, but broad asset stress unlikely: Report
briefs.deck: Nuvama Institutional Equities suggests that an RBI rate hike may not broadly impact NBFC asset quality. The report indicates that past rate increases did not lead to widespread deterioration. Current risks, including the West Asia conflict, appear limited to specific NBFC segments. Healthy capital buffers and liquidity may support overall asset quality for most NBFCs. Any future deterioration is…
briefs.bodyText:
A potential Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rate hike is unlikely to trigger broad-based stress in the asset quality of non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), with risks expected to remain concentrated in select segments unless monetary tightening is prolonged or accompanied by a major macroeconomic shock, Nuvama Institutional Equities said in its October report.
According to the report, NBFCs currently have healthy asset quality, while past trends indicate that rate hikes alone have not caused widespread deterioration.
“...monetary tightening by itself has not been sufficient to trigger a broad-based deterioration in NBFC asset quality,” Nuvama said. It added that “Stress has typically intensified when rate hikes have coincided with prolonged external shocks or funding/liquidity disruptions.”
Asset quality improved during previous tightening cycle
Nuvama noted that during the FY22-24 monetary tightening cycle, NBFC asset quality improved despite a 250-basis-point increase in the repo rate.
The improvement was supported by strong credit growth, higher write-offs, better underwriting and stronger provision buffers, the report said.
Citing RBI data, Nuvama said gross non-performing assets (GNPAs) declined from 5.7% in March 2022 to 4.6% in March 2023.
On current risks, the report said the impact of the West Asia conflict and global spillovers had so far remained limited to select segments of the NBFC sector.
“Importantly, the impact of the West-Asia conflict and global spill-overs has so far remained contained and confined to select low-ticket unsecured PL, BL, micro-LAP, and CV/CE segments,” it said.
Nuvama also flagged El Niño-related risks, saying these had remained limited so far but warranted monitoring as their impact could become visible with a lag if winter crops were affected.
Capital buffers, liquidity to support asset quality
The report said healthy capital and provision buffers across most NBFCs, along with abundant systemic liquidity and support for credit growth, were expected to cushion headline asset-quality ratios.
As a result, Nuvama said any deterioration was more likely to remain concentrated in specific segments or individual players rather than become broad-based.
“Any deterioration is more likely to remain pocketed and segment/player specific rather than broad-based, unless rate hikes become prolonged and are accompanied by a material external or macroeconomic shock,” it said, according to news agency ANI.
Rate cycle impact on NBFC margins
Nuvama also said the impact of the interest-rate cycle on NBFC profitability would vary depending on how quickly assets and liabilities reprice.
“The impact of a rate cycle on NBFC margins is unlikely to be uniform with the key differentiator being the mismatch between the repricing of existing assets-liabilities and incremental movement,” it said.

briefs.headline: RBI remains cautious on crypto, backs underlying technology: Governor Malhotra
briefs.deck: Governor Sanjay Malhotra says India supports innovation in distributed ledger technology and tokenisation, but is wary of cryptocurrencies over concerns about monetary sovereignty and capital flows
briefs.bodyText:
India has maintained a cautious approach towards cryptocurrencies while promoting the underlying technologies, such as distributed ledger technology and tokenisation, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra said on Saturday (October 3, 2026).
Mr. Malhotra said India supports innovation in the technologies underlying crypto assets, including distributed ledger and tokenisation, but remains cautious about cryptocurrencies, owing to concerns over monetary sovereignty, monetary policy and capital flows.
"So, our approach has been to promote the underlying technologies, and we are using some of these in the central bank and outside, in PPP [public-private partnership] mode. But insofar as crypto is concerned, it has been a cautious approach," he said at the Kautilya Economic Conclave.
Expressing concerns about cryptocurrencies, the RBI Governor said the issue was related to the "singleness of money" and their potential implications for monetary policy, particularly in emerging market economies, where capital flow restrictions are in place.
"The problem that you are trying to address is primarily not so much of domestic payments, because domestic payments within our country, and in many countries now, are quite fast, cheap and convenient," he said.
The more significant challenge is cross-border payments, for which other solutions, including central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), can be explored, Mr. Malhotra said.
On rising public debt and hardening bond yields globally, he said yield movement is essentially a function of demand and supply, with government and private-sector spending rising, including on account of artificial intelligence (AI). "Money is scarce, spending has increased, both by the government as well as private enterprises, led by AI, and so that's what is leading to the hardening of the bond yields and debts," he said.
Mr. Malhotra said the RBI's monetary policy primarily focuses on domestic growth-inflation dynamics, but that global interest rates also have implications for India, including through their impact on real interest rates in the country. "That is something that we need to take care of," he said.

briefs.headline: Could a mega US-Russia oil deal tied to Trump & his allies end Ukraine war?
briefs.bodyText:
Talks between the US and Russia over ending the war in Ukraine have expanded to include a proposed multibillion-dollar deal for Lukoil’s international oil assets, with the prospective investor group including people with business ties to US President Donald Trump’s allies. The deal would require approval from both the US government and the Kremlin.
The proposed transaction covers Lukoil’s overseas portfolio of oil fields, refineries and gas stations. A group led by US investor Todd Boehly has emerged as the leading bidder, alongside Middle Eastern investors and the US government. The details were reported by The New York Times, citing eight people familiar with the negotiations.
The negotiations have also brought renewed attention to the business links of Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who are leading US efforts to engage Moscow on the Ukraine war.
There is no indication that Witkoff or Kushner would personally profit from the proposed transaction. However, the deal has raised questions about the overlap between the Trump administration’s diplomatic efforts with Russia and the business interests of people connected to the president and his allies.
Putin raised Lukoil deal with US negotiators
Russian President Vladimir Putin raised the proposed Lukoil transaction when he met Witkoff and Kushner at the Kremlin on September 5, according to people familiar with the meeting.
Putin reportedly presented the deal as a potential way to demonstrate that Russian and US businesses could resume working together. The US side indicated it would work on the proposal, viewing it as a possible means of building goodwill with Moscow while potentially helping lower global energy prices.
The proposed sale would also benefit buyers because US approval could release the assets from American sanctions, increasing their value.
Lukoil’s international holdings include oil fields in Cameroon, refineries in Europe and gas stations in the US. While Lukoil is technically a private company, the decision over the deal is seen in Moscow as one that ultimately depends on Putin.
Who is seeking Lukoil’s assets
Boehly, co-owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers, is leading the group currently seeking the assets. He donated $1 million to MAGA Inc. in December 2025 and another $1 million through his investment firm to Trump’s inauguration.
The proposed investor group also includes Qatar-based businessmen Moutaz and Ramez Al-Khayyat and an Abu Dhabi investment fund controlled by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
The Al-Khayyat brothers have business ties with Kushner and his wife, Ivanka Trump, including a planned luxury resort project in Albania.
Sheikh Tahnoon controls an investment fund that acquired a significant stake in World Liberty Financial, the Trump family-linked cryptocurrency company co-founded by Witkoff. Trump’s sons are also involved in the company. Witkoff has since sold his stake, according to a person close to him.
Sheikh Tahnoon also oversees Lunate, an Abu Dhabi investment fund that is among the major stakeholders in the private equity firm founded by Kushner after he left the White House.
US approval remains crucial
The Lukoil deal is not final and requires approval from the US treasury department, which oversees sanctions enforcement.
The Trump administration had sanctioned Lukoil in October 2025 as part of measures targeting Russia’s energy sector and pressing Moscow over the Ukraine war.
A senior US administration official said, as quoted by NYT, Witkoff and Kushner had directly participated in negotiating the financial terms of the proposed US government investment, including “a substantial upfront payment and profits interest for the United States.”
Previous Lukoil bid stalled
The Lukoil assets have attracted several potential buyers since the company put its international holdings on the market.
US private equity firm Carlyle reached a tentative agreement in January to acquire a large portion of the assets, but US approval for that bid stalled. The Boehly-led group subsequently emerged as the leading bidder.
The treasury department has had to repeatedly extend sanctions-related arrangements while the sale remains unresolved. The latest extension is due to run until October 29.
Lukoil valued its international assets at about $20 billion earlier this year, although the price and structure of the proposed transaction have not been disclosed.
The proposed sale comes as the Trump administration seeks to use the prospect of renewed economic ties with Russia as part of its broader effort to persuade Moscow to compromise over Ukraine. Witkoff and Kushner have repeatedly travelled to Russia for talks with Putin as Washington pursues an end to the war.

stories.headline: 'My goal is to have 3': Alex Albon wants Thailand to join his list of F1 home races
stories.deck: Alex Albon considers Singapore and Malaysia his two Formula 1 home races, but the Williams driver wants Thailand to join that list. With Thailand targeting a potential F1 race in Bangkok from 2028, Albon’s Thai heritage could give him a third home event. Speaking to the Times of India ahead of the Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang, Albon also discussed his growing role in developing Williams’ future…
stories.bodyText:
Representing your country or continent on the biggest stage is a blessing, which Atlassian Williams F1 driver Alex Albon feels about his Thai heritage, which has given him an identity and the respect of fans across Southeast Asia. Williams driver considers both Malaysia and Singapore as “home races” and hopes Thailand can eventually join that list.
Malaysia is hosting the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang this weekend as part of an arrangement that keeps the Bahrain round on the Formula 1 calendar. The race will be this weekend, with Sepang serving as Round 16 of the 2026 F1 season.
For Albon, the venue carries significance beyond the unusual circumstances surrounding this year’s race. He races under the Thai flag and has a strong connection with Southeast Asia, where he feels particularly embraced by fans.
“It’s lovely to kind of be able to say that I have two home races, which are Singapore and Malaysia. In the end, my goal would be to have three, which is obviously Thailand as well,” Albon told the Times of India in a roundtable interaction ahead of this weekend’s Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
“I feel like I get very embraced by Southeast Asian fans in general. I feel very lucky.”
Albon said his Thai heritage has given him greater exposure across the region, with Malaysia and Thailand sharing a particularly strong connection.
“I would say in terms of my identity, more than anything, it just gives me more exposure,” Albon said when asked how his Thai heritage has shaped his identity in Formula 1.
“I find that the Southeast Asian grouping of countries is kind of like one big family in many ways. And having, for example, Malaysia as another home race is amazing. I feel especially Malaysia and Thailand have a very strong connection, very strong relationship,” he added.
Thailand could give Albon a third home race
Albon’s wish to see Thailand join the Formula 1 calendar could become a reality as early as 2028.
Thailand has approved a $1.23 billion bid to host an F1 street race in Bangkok, with the proposed race expected to run under an initial five-year contract from 2028 to 2032.
The proposed 5.7-kilometre street circuit will feature 18 corners and run through the Bangkok area between Krung Thep Aphiwat Central Terminal Station and Chatuchak Park. The race is being considered for either March or September, depending on its eventual place on the F1 calendar.
For now, Albon has Malaysia and Singapore.
The 5.543-kilometre Sepang circuit features 15 corners and will host a 56-lap Grand Prix on Sunday. The race is scheduled to begin at 3pm local time on October 4, with qualifying taking place on Saturday at 4pm.
Sepang previously hosted Formula 1 from 1999 to 2017 and is known for its long straights, technical corners and unpredictable weather.
The Malaysian weekend also gives Albon another chance to race in front of fans from a region he increasingly regards as home.
Albon on the growing role of drivers in F1 development
Albon’s responsibilities at Williams extend beyond what happens once he gets behind the wheel.
The Thai-British driver, who made his F1 debut in 2019 and returned to the grid with Williams in 2022, said his experience has seen him become increasingly involved in projects for future cars and in discussions with engineers about the direction of development.
“I feel more and more involved in the process and the projects leading into next year’s cars, with experience, you take on more accountability and also you develop a trust with the engineers together as well, that they can kind of, I guess, believe in what you say and the direction that you want the car to go in,” Albon said.
He believes having two experienced drivers can also help a team identify weaknesses in a car and push development forward.
“I think it’s very fortunate for us as a team that we have two drivers that are experienced. And I think that does allow us to be able to lean on each other, lean on the team and push the development forward,” he said.
Albon pointed to the challenge teams can face when both drivers are rookies.
“If you have two rookies, it’s a lot harder to understand what are the weak points of the car,” he said.
But experience in Formula 1, according to Albon, is not simply about the number of seasons a driver has spent on the grid. It is also about knowing how to communicate with the right people within a team.
“The biggest difference is actually the maturity as a driver to speak to the relevant people within the team, to go directly to them and to discuss how to get better as a group,” he said.
“These kind of areas, I feel like every year I’ve become more and more involved in, which I enjoy. I think it’s a part of Formula One that doesn’t get talked about a lot, but the driver has a big involvement in the way the car gets developed,” he concluded.
Sepang first, Singapore next
After the Malaysian weekend, F1 heads to Singapore from October 9-11, giving Albon another opportunity to race in a part of the world he considers home. The Singapore Grand Prix will be held at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.
For now, two home races remain on Albon’s list. But with Thailand working towards a place on the F1 calendar, the Williams driver has already made clear what he would like to see next.

stories.headline: Shubman Gill equals MS Dhoni, Yuvraj Singh to enter elite India club
stories.deck: Shubman Gill has successfully equaled the impressive record of MS Dhoni, achieving seven Player of the Series awards in ODIs. This remarkable feat was accomplished following India's recent series victory against the West Indies, where Gill scored 110 runs and an incredible unbeaten 233 in the first two matches. Despite a loss in the third match, his consistent performance places him among legends…
stories.bodyText:
Shubman Gill
 continued to strengthen his credentials as one of India's most consistent performers in ODI cricket, equalling 
MS Dhoni
's tally of seven Player of the Series awards after India's three-match series against the West Indies on Saturday.
Gill's latest recognition came despite India losing the third ODI by five wickets, with the hosts winning the series 2-1. The Indian captain scored a century in the opening match and followed it up with a double hundred in the second, both innings coming while chasing.
Gill struck 110 in the first ODI before producing a stunning unbeaten 233 in the second. His performances helped India secure the series before the West Indies bounced back with a record chase in the final match.
With seven Player of the Series awards, Gill has now drawn level with Dhoni among Indian players. He also matches Yuvraj Singh and Sourav Ganguly, while 
Virat Kohli
 has 11 such awards and Sachin Tendulkar leads the list with 15.
What makes Gill's record particularly striking is the period in which he has achieved it. All seven of his Player of the Series awards have come since 2022. No other Indian player has won more than three in the same period, underlining his consistency across bilateral ODI contests.
The West Indies, however, ensured India did not complete a clean sweep. Shai Hope's unbeaten 162 powered the visitors to 352 for five, their highest successful ODI chase, after India posted 351 for seven.
KL Rahul's unbeaten 129 and Rohit Sharma's 92 had put India in a commanding position, but Hope's masterclass secured a consolation victory for the visitors.
India nevertheless took the series 2-1, with Gill's remarkable run across the first two matches earning him another individual milestone and drawing him level with one of India's most celebrated former captains.

stories.headline: Ireland press conference ahead of Israel game in Nations League cut short
stories.deck: Ireland defeated Israel 3-0 last Sunday (September 27, 2026) but only after Irish players took a vote on whether or not to go ahead with the game, due to bitter opposition in Ireland over Israel's actions in Gaza
stories.bodyText:
Ireland's press conference ahead of its contentious Nations League game against Israel was abruptly ended Saturday (October 3, 2026) when a journalist asked coach Heimir Hallgrimsson about alleged racism by Irish players during last week's match between the teams.
Ireland defeated Israel 3-0 last Sunday (September 27, 2026) but only after Irish players took a vote on whether or not to go ahead with the game, due to bitter opposition in Ireland over Israel's actions in Gaza.
On Saturday (October 3, 2026), an Israeli journalist alleged that Irish players made racist comments, which promoted an immediate rebuke from Football Association of Ireland communications manager Kieran Crowley: “That's completely untrue.” The press conference was then ended.
Sunday's (October 4, 2026) game — Ireland is the “home” team — is being held in Backa Topola, Serbia, without any fans present.
The FAI moved the game to an neutral venue for “operational reasons” in June following widespread calls in Ireland for a boycott. It also followed the FAI's own motion the previous November calling on UEFA to ban Israel from club and international competitions.
The FAI has resisted calls for a boycott, arguing the team could be hit with sanctions by UEFA. Ireland is co-hosting the 2028 European Championship with England, Wales and Scotland.
Last Sunday's game was held in Debrecen, Hungary, where Irish players wore black armbands. The FAI was investigating whether Ireland forward Adam Idah was racially abused during the match. A small number of Israel supporters had attended.
On Thursday, Ireland's game against Austria in Dublin was briefly interrupted by protesters throwing tennis balls bearing Palestinian flags.

stories.headline: Vithya Ramraj’s record run: How far has India come in the 400m hurdles?
stories.deck: She broke P.T. Usha’s 42-year-old record to win bronze, while also anchoring India to gold in the women’s 4×400m relay and silver in the mixed 4×400m relay. Vithya’s coach, Nehpal Singh Rathore, explains why she needed to train for both the 400m hurdles and the flat.
stories.bodyText:
As Vithya Ramraj entered the final stretch of the 400m hurdles in Aichi-Nagoya, the race for gold was still open for India at the 2026 Asian Games. Vithya and the UAE’s Mariam Kareem were neck-and-neck over the final two hurdles, with Kazakhstan’s Adelina Zems just behind them. But at the last hurdle, Vithya lost some ground as Mariam surged ahead to take gold in a Games-record 54.31 seconds, while Adelina moved past Vithya to claim silver in 54.58. The Indian crossed the line third in 54.75.
But by then, the colour of the medal had become almost secondary. Vithya had done what she had been trying to do since 2023, when she equalled P.T. Usha’s 55.42-second national record that had stood for more than 40 years. She was 0.67 seconds faster than Usha and became the first Indian woman to break the 55-second barrier in the 400m hurdles. “I met Usha ma’am a year ago, and she said, ‘Go for 54 seconds.’ She encouraged me. So doing this today makes me so happy,” the 28-year-old said.
She is now the fastest Indian woman in the event, but her record places her 187th on the all-time world list.
That list is led by Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone, followed by Femke Bol and Dalilah Muhammad, whose bests are 50.37, 50.95 and 51.58 seconds, respectively. She remains more than four seconds behind the world’s fastest mark, but has moved from 56th before the Asiad to 35th in the current world rankings, putting her among the leading athletes in the event today.
Moreover, the record places her among a relatively small group of the fastest performances in Asia, ranking 12th on the continent. Bahrain’s Kemi Adekoya leads the regional list, while athletes from China, Kazakhstan and the UAE also feature prominently. The regional landscape was very different when Usha set her record in 1984. Until then, the 55-second barrier had been breached only by European athletes, with one African athlete also having gone under the mark. In fact, Usha remained the only Asian performance on the list until 1990 because World Athletics’ historical list captures performances faster than 57.3 seconds only. Since then, the depth of competition in Asia has grown considerably, with 12 performances now under 55 seconds.
These broader improvements in performance have coincided with a steady progression in Vithya’s own performances. Her best in the 400m hurdles was 59.7 seconds in 2018, which improved to 56.57 in 2022. In 2023, she matched Usha’s record. Her best then stood at 56.04 in 2025, before she made her biggest improvement yet in 2026.
Her coach, Nepal Singh Rathore, believes the progression in the hurdles cannot be separated from her improvement in the flat 400m. When Vithya began training under him, her coach said other coaches questioned why she was being prepared for both events. “Only when she runs well in the flat, she can run hurdles well. Because speed plays a major role in all events,” he told The Hindu, explaining his approach.
And the progression in the two events, he added, has followed the same pattern: “Whenever she has improved in the flats, she has improved in the hurdles.” Vithya’s best time in that event improved from 54.48 seconds in 2018 to 51.96 seconds in 2026. Over the same period, her hurdles best fell by nearly five seconds, from 59.70 to 54.75.
The versatility her coach had sought to build through that training approach was on full display in her overall Asian Games campaign. She won a medal of each colour, anchoring India to gold in the women’s 4×400m relay and silver in the mixed 4×400m relay, alongside her record-breaking bronze.
Note: The data for the charts were sourced from World Athletics.

briefs.headline: Who is Witty Alien? The 'shirtless guy' who shocked world No. 1 Carlsen
briefs.deck: Bulgarian chess creator Volen Dyulgerov, known as Witty Alien, stunned world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen in a blitz game during Chess.com’s Chess Club Showdown. The 27-year-old Candidate Master, known for his energetic content and Alien Gambit, has a 2181 FIDE rating. Despite Carlsen’s much higher online rating, Dyulgerov secured a memorable upset victory in the event.
briefs.bodyText:
Magnus Carlsen
, widely regarded as one of the greatest chess players ever, recently suffered a surprise defeat in a blitz game against Bulgarian chess creator Volen Dyulgerov, better known online as Witty Alien or the "shirtless guy" these days.
The upset happened on September 30 during Chess.com’s first Chess Club Showdown.
Who is Witty Alien?
Dyulgerov, born in 1999, is a Candidate Master (CM) from Bulgaria. His highest FIDE rating was 2200, reached in 2023, while his rating stood at 2181 in September 2026.
Although he is a decent over-the-board player, he has become much more popular through online chess and content creation.
Known for his energetic personality, Witty Alien has built a following on YouTube and online chess platforms.
Chess.com named him Creator of the Month in July 2024 and credited him with the popular Alien Gambit.
His Chess.com blitz rating is around 2612, while Carlsen’s is about 3396, making the victory even more unexpected.
 Magnus Carlsen was visibly stunned
The game, which ended in the five-time world champion visibly looking stunned after the defeat to the Bulgarian, was part of the Chess Club Showdown, a two-hour five-minute blitz event featuring nine chess clubs.
Amateur players had the chance to face major stars such as Carlsen, Maxime Vachier-Lagrave and Anish Giri.
Carlsen represented Team Liquid Chess Club, which finished second in the main arena with 2312 points. 9z Globant topped the standings with 2368 points and later won the final 53.5-45.5.
Also Read: ‘
Sometimes in chess, there are just these blind spots’: Nihal Sarin looks back at his Chess Olympiad loss to Uzbekistan | Exclusive
Carlsen managed to win both of his games on board one during the final, but he had already suffered a defeat earlier in the event. That loss came against Witty Alien, who produced one of the biggest surprises of the tournament by taking down the world-class Norwegian in blitz.

briefs.headline: ‘Great man MS Dhoni’: Hope reveals advice that helped him script record chase
briefs.deck: Shai Hope played a pivotal role in West Indies' remarkable success against India by scoring an unbeaten 162. His innings helped the team chase down a daunting target of 352 runs with ten balls to spare. After India's innings, bolstered by KL Rahul’s 129, Hope drew inspiration from MS Dhoni to pace his batting.
briefs.bodyText:
Shai Hope
 turned to advice from former India captain 
MS Dhoni
 to pace his innings as West Indies chased down their highest-ever ODI target against India and signed off the series with a five-wicket win on Saturday.
Hope produced an unbeaten 162 off 143 balls, his second successive century in the series, to guide West Indies to 352-5 in 48.2 overs after India posted 351-7. The visitors completed the chase with 10 balls to spare, ending India's winning streak in the series after defeats in Thiruvananthapuram and Guwahati.
Speaking after being named Player of the Match, Hope revealed that a conversation with 
Dhoni
 had influenced the way he approached the chase.
"Something that I had a great chat with the great man MS Dhoni, he was telling you always have more time than you think," Hope said.
"Just trying not to focus too much on the end result. Just look at the process, try to break the game down as best as I can and find ways to get the boundaries in the back end."
The advice proved particularly valuable given the circumstances. Hope had promoted himself to opener after Jewel Andrew reportedly injured a finger while taking a catch and was taken to hospital. 
He had also spent the entire 50 overs behind the stumps in high humidity before walking out to bat.
West Indies were also a batter short, while Hope said the team could effectively have been two down with Vitel Lawes unavailable.
"It would always be a challenge," Hope said. "So just trying not to focus too much on the end result."
Hope reached his 50 off 46 balls and brought up his 21st ODI hundred from 104 deliveries. He then shifted gears dramatically, scoring 62 runs from his final 39 balls.
After Keemo Paul fell in the 41st over, Hope added 62 off 29 balls with Gudakesh Motie to take West Indies over the line. India's slow over rate meant the hosts had to have an additional fielder inside the 30-yard circle for the final four overs, something Hope had anticipated.
"I even thought about the overs that the Indian team were behind. So I knew they would have to bring a couple fielders in, in the back end," he said.
"It's always tough when you're trying to defend a score and you got to have five men in the ring. So all those things I calculated when I was batting. Just so happened that everything worked out for us in the back end."
Hope also revealed that he began feeling discomfort around his groin after about 30 overs of the chase but decided to push through.
"Probably about 30 overs in, felt a little something in the groin area. So just tried to fight to the end there," he said.
He fittingly struck the winning run, completing a remarkable chase that gave West Indies their highest successful run chase in ODI cricket.
India's total had been built around KL Rahul's unbeaten 129 off 87 balls, while Rohit Sharma made 92. But Hope's marathon effort ensured West Indies finally had something to celebrate after India had already sealed the three-match series with two convincing wins.

briefs.headline: 'Doing things for social media': Ex-Pak player slams Ayub for Sooryavanshi send-off
briefs.deck: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the Asian Games final, but controversy followed Saim Ayub’s ‘baby cradle’ send-off to 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Former Pakistan player Kamran Akmal criticised the gesture, saying players should focus on performances rather than social media attention. India posted 211/6, while Hasan Nawaz’s 96 couldn’t prevent Pakistan’s defeat.
briefs.bodyText:
India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the Asian Games men’s cricket final on Saturday, but the match was much closer than the final score suggests. Pakistan, led by Sahibzada Farhan, pushed India hard, with Hasan Nawaz scoring 96.
India eventually held its nerve in the final overs through 
Jasprit Bumrah
 and 
Shivam Dube
 to retain the gold medal.
The match also saw controversy when Pakistan all-rounder 
Saim Ayub
 dismissed 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 15 off nine balls.
After taking the wicket, Ayub appeared to make a ‘baby cradle’ gesture, which was seen as a send-off directed at the young Indian batter. Sooryavanshi did not react and simply returned to the dugout.
Kamran Akmal criticises Saim Ayub
Former Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Kamran Akmal criticised Ayub’s celebration during a discussion on the ‘Game Plan’ YouTube show.
The presenter questioned the gesture and said, “Did you see that action? How unfortunate is that? You are playing such good cricket. You are giving India competition after such a long time. These things don't look good.”
Akmal agreed with the criticism and said, “These things have been happening for a long time. Our performance hasn't been great, but we are doing things for social media. The management should think about this. 
It's international cricket. No matter whether he is 13, 14 or 15, he's playing international cricket. Saim Ayub is not a kid. He should focus on his performances.”
Sooryavanshi made a quick start
Sooryavanshi had started aggressively, hitting Saad Masood for two sixes in the second over. However, his attempt to play a reverse sweep against Ayub ended his innings.
India posted 211/6, with Abhishek Sharma scoring 61, Tilak Varma making an unbeaten 51 and Shivam Dube contributing 27. Pakistan fought back through Hasan Nawaz and Ayub, but India pulled away in the final two overs.
Dube played a key role as India secured a 19-run victory and successfully defended its Asian Games title.

briefs.headline: India vs. West Indies third ODI: Hope leads from the front as West Indies prevents clean sweep
briefs.deck: The skipper scores his second century on the bounce as the Caribbean outfit chases down the target of 352 with 10 balls to spare
briefs.bodyText:
West Indies coach Daren Sammy, on the eve of the third and final ODI against India, said a win against the world’s top-ranked side would give his team the much-needed confidence at a time when the players brace for pay cuts back home.
On Saturday, Shai Hope made his coach’s wish come true, leading from the front with an inspirational unbeaten 162 (143b, 17x4, 3x6) to guide his side to a five-wicket win and salvage pride by avoiding a whitewash at the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium.
Chasing 352, Hope, opening the batting, scored his second century on the bounce as the Caribbean outfit hunted down the target with 10 balls to spare.
Hope set the tone in the PowerPlay with exquisitely timed shots through covers, down the ground, and off the pads. The skipper, along with Amir Jangoo (67, 56b, 5x4, 1x6), the other centurion from the second ODI in Guwahati, stitched together a 109-run stand for the second wicket off just 99 deliveries.
The Indian bowlers looked flat and struggled to create chances in dewy conditions. However, against the run of play, Jangoo was run out when his partner sent him back. Keemo Paul chipped in, scoring a quickfire 44 (35b, 5x4). Once Paul departed, Hope dug deep despite battling fatigue. With the asking rate climbing above 11, Hope swatted Kuldeep for a six and a four in the 46th over. He followed it up with a brace of boundaries off Gurnoor Brar and Anshul Kamboj and, in the process, brought up his 150 as well.
Earlier, India posted 351 for seven, riding on K.L. Rahul’s well-paced unbeaten 129 (87b, 10x4, 6x6).
Electing to bat, the Men in Blue were rocked early in the third over when Jayden Seales struck twice. He had Gill caught down the leg-side and cleaned up Virat Kohli with an in-dipper that uprooted the middle-stump.
Rohit Sharma (92, 85b, 10x4, 3x6) and Ruturaj Gaikwad (57, 69b, 1x4, 4x6) steadied the innings with a 137-run stand. The former started cautiously against a disciplined opening burst from Seales and Matthew Forde before shifting gears.
After Rohit’s departure, Rahul took charge. The latter hit boundaries through conventional strokes, the best being the straight drive off Seales. During his knock, Rahul surpassed 10,000 international runs. At the back end of the innings, he showcased his repertoire and brought up his ninth ODI ton in style, pulling Seales over fine-leg for a maximum.
However, on this day, Hope did spring eternal for West Indies.

briefs.headline: IND vs BRA friendly: From Chennai to Bhopal, Brazil supporters bring samba flair to Kolkata
briefs.deck: Brazil supporters from across India and beyond travelled to Kolkata for a rare chance to watch the Samba Boys play India and painted the Salt Lake Stadium yellow and green.
briefs.bodyText:
TimesofIndia.com in Kolkata:
 People from different walks of life made their way to the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata for the historic India versus Brazil friendly. Even though the iconic venue wasn't filled to its 65,000 capacity, many were still keen on making the most of this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. A family of six from Chennai. A Brazilian living in Delhi. A family with two young boys from Delhi. Another family had travelled from Bhopal with their two daughters.
Kohana had her husband and four boys for company. They went through India and Brazil jerseys on the street adjacent to the venue. The father went through them one by one while the four boys tested the size by placing the jerseys against themselves.
"We live in Chennai but we're from Japan. We bought tickets last week and have travelled just for this match. I'm supporting both teams today but the boys are big fans of the Brazilian team," said Kohana, who hails from Osaka, with a smile.
"We wanted to stay for the Uruguay game also but because they have school next week, we'll do just the Brazil match," she said, referring to the next FIFA friendly on October 6.
Kohana, her husband and four boys travelled from Chennai to Kolkata for the India vs Brazil game. (Image: Tanuj Lakhina/TimesofIndia.com)
Forty-six-year-old Felipe, who comes from Porto Alegre, the birthplace of Ronaldinho, has taken the trip from New Delhi. 
He works in the tourism sector in the capital with the aim of bringing more Brazilians, like himself, to travel to India.
The moment he heard about the match, he didn't hesitate to buy a ticket online. Mere hours after arriving in Kolkata, he was overwhelmed by the city's food offerings.
"I never thought Brazil would come here. When I saw the Brazilian team was coming to India, I decided that no matter what, no matter how, I have to be there. I have to see this match," he said, revealing that he had spent around €150 on the ticket (Rs 16,000).
Felipe, who is a Brazilian national, currently lives in Delhi. (Image: Tanuj Lakhina/TimesofIndia.com)
"I like the city. I like the food, it is very good. I went to the Victoria Memorial, it's beautiful. I went to the New Market, a lot of things to see and buy," he continued.
Adeeba and Aneefa Warsi donned the yellow and green of Brazil as they readied themselves outside the Salt Lake Stadium. Adeeba sported some bling to go with the outfit and had the colours of India and Brazil painted on both cheeks. The two sisters from Bhopal were joined by their parents for this big contest.
For Aneefa, this wasn't just about watching India or Brazil play. It was also a chance for her, a footballer herself, to learn some things from the professionals.
Sisters Adeeba and Aneefa Warsi live in Bhopal. They made the India vs Brazil friendly into a football-tourism activity alongside their parents.  (Image: Tanuj Lakhina/TimesofIndia.com)
"I hope to get inspired by the players and learn some new stuff. This is my first time watching a match, so I want to get better also," she said.
Her elder sister chimed in by saying, "For me, this is an outing as well. I watch football also, so this is an experience for me also. So I want to see the scope of football in the country and take up the sport myself in the future," said the first-year college student.
For the past month, since the tickets were bought, the duo spent sleepless nights. The preparations had begun well in advance. Even a night ago, as they arrived in the city, the match remained the topic of conversation.
"When to buy the jersey, where to buy it from? What kind of makeup to do? What look to show? What to wear? Everything was considered in the past month," explained Adeeba.

briefs.headline: Hope battles cramps as WI chase down 352 to beat India by 5 wickets
briefs.deck: Hope overshadowed KL Rahul’s counterattacking unbeaten 129 off 87 balls that propelled India to 351/7. Dew may have played a part, but Hope’s experience tamed down India’s inexperienced bowling with consummate ease
briefs.bodyText:
New Chandigarh: India’s ODI team is in a phase where it is on the lookout for stern challenges to identify its own core group for the World Cup in South Africa, which is a year away. After two lopsided victories in the first two ODIs, India were finally tested by West Indies for the entire length of the match, which ended with captain Shai Hope’s effortless unbeaten 162 off 143 balls chasing down 352-run target with 10 balls and five wickets remaining.
Coming out to open the batting, Hope overshadowed KL Rahul’s counterattacking unbeaten 129 off 87 balls that propelled India to 351/7. Dew may have played a part, but Hope’s experience tamed down India’s inexperienced bowling with consummate ease as the West Indies team pulled one back in the series to soothe the pain of the impending pay cuts in their match fees.
India’s greatest challenge coming into the series was to identify a backup pace attack to complement Jasprit Bumrah. The team management may have to wait a little longer to nail the pace attack.
Be it the pace and movement up front in the match or Hope’s unwavering temperament in the chase, India were always playing catch-up. When Jayden Seales breached Virat Kohli’s defence immediately after removing 
Shubman Gill
 off the previous ball in the third over of the match, the conditions seemed like what one may expect in South Africa in a year’s time. If ever the selectors needed an affirmation about Rohit Sharma’s capability to survive and dominate in testing conditions, his carefully paced knock of 92 off 85 to put India back on track did just that.
After the first 10 overs of the match, where India laboured to 32/2, Rohit broke free along with Ruturaj Gaikwad to resume the usual business of brisk run-scoring. India kept losing wickets at regular intervals, but the scoring rate maintained an upward trajectory till they finished with 351/7.
As has been the trend in the series, run scoring never looked challenging for the batters. Just like India cruised to victory while chasing big totals in the previous two games, West Indies batters too looked fairly untroubled in the evening. The only thing that troubled Hope was running between the wickets with cramps. Had Amir Jangoo not been run out for 67 off 56, things would have moved at a faster rate for West Indies.
Rahul’s innings did have a couple of dropped catches in it, but his fluency was such that one couldn’t make out this was his only outing with the bat in the series. Rahul faces stiff competition from Ishan Kishan for holding on to his spot in the XI. Saturday’s knock will improve his stocks as the lead wicketkeeper in the team.

briefs.headline: Brazil’s quality too good for India
briefs.deck: Chelsea winger Estevao scored Brazil’s first goal and ‌assisted Pedro before Lino netted a second-half brace, helping Carlo Ancelotti’s side ‌conclude their tour of Australia and India ‌with ⁠two wins and a draw
briefs.bodyText:
India showed fight and intent, but Brazil’s attacking quality proved too hot to handle as the South American giant ran out a 4-0 winner in the historic international friendly at the Salt Lake Stadium on Saturday (October 3, 2026).
India held its shape in the opening 25 minutes but was hesitant to commit numbers into the attacking third, leaving Brazilian goalkeeper Pedro Morisco with little to do.
Apuia had a crack at goal in the seventh minute, but his effort was off target. Eight minutes later, Bijoy Varghese played a delightful ball over the top to Manvir Singh, who timed his run perfectly and found himself through on goal. Brazil captain Marquinhos, however, tracked back brilliantly to nick the ball away.
At the other end, Vinicius Junior began to turn on the style. The Real Madrid star made three attempts in the first eight minutes, but right-back Abhishek Singh stood his ground to deny him on the first two occasions. Vinicius then cut inside onto his right foot and got his shot away, only for Gurpreet Singh Sandhu to produce a save.
Gurpreet came to India’s rescue again in the 20th minute when Vinicius broke into the box, with the Indian captain blocking his effort.
Brazil’s pace and movement eventually stretched the Indian defence. Estevao broke the deadlock in the 28th minute, cutting in from the right before unleashing a fierce left-footed shot. Gurpreet appeared well positioned, but had no answer to the powerful strike as the ball deflected off his hand and nestled into the net.
The goal opened up more space for Brazil, and Pedro doubled the advantage in the 42nd minute with an angled drive. Gurpreet got a hand to it, but he spilled the ball and it crossed the line.
Brazil made five changes at half-time, but the intensity did not drop. Samuel Lino, brought on for Vinicius, scored twice after the break (58th and 90+5) as Brazil completed a comfortable victory.
For Khalid Jamil’s India, the scoreline does not reflect the encouraging intent it showed early in the game. This experience definitely gave the hosts a taste of football at the highest level. With both sides agreeing to make a maximum of 11 substitutions, a majority of the Indian squad got the opportunity to experience the Brazilian flair from close quarters and share the pitch with some of the biggest names in world football.
The result: India 0 lost to Brazil 4 (Estevao 28, Pedro 42, Samuel Lino 58, 90+5).

briefs.headline: Asian Games 2026: Ice-cool Kumkum strikes historic recurve gold, earns Olympic quota
briefs.deck: Kumkum Mohod became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal in the individual recurve event.
briefs.bodyText:
A 17-year-old single-handedly broke the Korean hegemony and set a new benchmark for Indian recurve archery going forward on Saturday (October 3, 2026). Kumkum Mohod kept hitting the target for India’s first ever individual gold in the event at the Asian Games, overcoming two Koreans and a Chinese opponent en route to her second gold in her maiden outing.
Against Tokyo Olympics gold medalist and reigning World Champion Kang Chaeyoung in the quarterfinals, Kumkum took the first set 29-28 before a series of nines saw her losing the second 27-28 for Kang to go level. The scoreline was reversed in the next set and with both scoring 29 each in the fourth set, Kumkum kept the lead 5-3 going into the decider.
Keep track | Asian Games 2026 LIVE: Archer Kumkum wins historic recurve gold at Asian Games, earns Olympic quota
The fifth and final set saw Kang starting off and shooting a 28 with a 10, rounding off with two nines. The two nines were matched on the first two shots, leaving Kumkum needing a 10 on her final shot to get one point for a tied set and the win and ensure the game didn’t go into a shoot-off. Steady as a rock, the 17-year-old duly delivered, winning 6-4.
Kumkum had destroyed The Destroyer, Kang’s nickname in archery circles. One down, two more to go. Next up was China’s reigning World Championships silver medalist Zhu Jingyi who, at 20, is already being spoken of the next big thing in the sport. Kumkum would have none of it.
She completely dominated the match all the way. Zhu started the proceedings, and the pressure was visible, scoring an eight on her very first arrow. Kumkum took the lead with a 28-27, then tied the next two sets, both scoring 30 and 29 each. In the fourth set, Zhu managed a total of 28. Kumkum started with a 9 on her 13th arrow, then closed it out with a couple of 10s to take the match 6-2 and storm into the final, becoming the first Indian woman ever to do so.
But she wasn’t done yet. There was one more to go, another Korean, another 20-year-old Oh Yejin. It was the one that mattered; it was the closest in terms of competition, and the pressure took its toll with both trading leads. Kumkum shot her first eight of the competition on her 3rd arrow to lose the first set with a 27, then shot a 29 to tie the second. A perfect 30 helped her take the third and go level 3-3. Another 8 on her 11th arrow saw her trail 5-3 in the 4th set, making the 5th a must-win situation.
Pressure clearly brings out the best from the youngster. Three hits bang to the centre meant the onus was on Oh now to match. She got two nines plus a 10 and it was single-arrow shoot-off time. Oh stumbled for an eight. Kumkum found the middle with a 10, and a shy smile was all there to indicate the magnitude of her achievement.
The men, however, had to settle for a bronze after a face-off between compatriots Neeraj Chauhan and Dhiraj Bommadevara, both going down in their respective semifinals before Neeraj outshot his senior teammate 6-4 for a podium finish.
